# Astryx catalogue (0.7.12)

suzuri's chrome (everything around the terminal panes) is built with
[Astryx](https://astryx.atmeta.com), Meta's MIT design system, theme Neutral.
Before building any UI, pick from what is listed here; don't hand-roll a
control Astryx already has.

- Live, searchable: `npm run astryx -- search <words>` in `ui/`
  (`component <Name>`, `hook <name>`, `template <id>`, `docs <topic>`).
  Never run a bare `npx astryx`: that name is an unrelated npm package.
- This folder is a snapshot of the same docs at 0.7.12, regenerated by
  `npm run astryx-catalog` in `ui/` after an upgrade.

| [BottomSheet](components/BottomSheet.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/BottomSheet` | [BottomSheetSwitcher](components/BottomSheetSwitcher.md) | A mobile touch surface for filters, actions, forms, and detail views that should rise from the bottom of the viewport. For a multi-step flow, give each step its own sheet and one state value that names the open step (see Replacing a sheet); open a second sheet over the first when a step should stay visible beneath it. Stacking. Every sheet keeps its own isOpen. Open a sheet while another scrim sheet is open and it stacks on top: the sheet beneath stays mounted with its scroll position and inputs, recedes behind the new one (the nearest covered sheet shrinks to 0.96 and lifts 8px, deeper ones to 0.92 and 16px), and is blocked from pointer, keyboard, and assistive technology by the top sheet's modal dialog. The sheets can be siblings, live in separate components, sit inside another sheet's content, or sit inside a BottomSheetSwitcher step; a whole switcher is one level, and switching its step in place does not change its position. Nothing moves in the DOM: each sheet's dialog stays where it is written, and no wrapper component is needed. Order is open order. The top sheet is the one presented most recently that is still open; a sheet that closes and reopens comes back on top. When several sheets open in one update (a deep link into a flow), there is no open order between them, so tree order decides: a sheet below the sheets rendered in its content, siblings in the order they are written. That order is right in the first painted frame. One scrim. Only the bottom sheet's backdrop dims the page; the backdrops of the sheets above it are transparent, so a stack never darkens per level. The dim holds steady while sheets push and pop, and if the bottom sheet closes while sheets remain above it, the next sheet's backdrop takes over in the same frame. Dismissal. Escape, a tap on the scrim, a downward swipe, and a platform close request (Android back, a close watcher) reach only the top sheet, through that sheet's own onOpenChange, and that sheet's purpose applies: required blocks all of them, form blocks the scrim and the swipe. Nothing closes a whole stack at once; set every sheet closed in one update when a flow is done and they leave together. Closing a covered sheet from code. Sheets rendered inside the closing sheet's content are part of it: they are presented only while it is open and leave with it. Their isOpen stays yours, as with a Dialog rendered in a closed Dialog: nothing is written to it, and a nested sheet that is still open when its host reopens is presented again, on top. Set it closed yourself when the flow is done. Sheets above the closing sheet that are not in its content stay open and keep their order; the closing sheet slides out from beneath them, and if it owned the scrim, the sheet above takes it over. Replacing a sheet. Close the top sheet and open another in the same update (one state value that names the open step does this) and the new sheet replaces it instead of stacking on it: the new sheet rises above the one it replaces; if the replaced sheet is taller it moves down to meet the new sheet's top edge at the same time; the replaced sheet fades only after both motions finish, and is inert and hidden from assistive technology from the start. The scrim holds steady throughout, with no dip; focus moves into the new sheet; and when the flow closes, focus returns to the element that opened its first sheet, whichever sheet closed last. This is the handoff the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher ran between its steps; a multi-step flow needs no switcher: give each step its own BottomSheet and one state value. A replace happens only when exactly one sheet closes and one opens in the update, the closing sheet was the top sheet of its stack, and the move was made from inside it (the control last pressed, or with no recent press the focused element, was in the closing sheet, as a step's own Continue or Back button is); a covered sheet closing while a sheet opens, a close and an open in different updates, or a close and an open driven from a control outside the closing sheet (two unrelated owners acting at once) keep the ordinary push and pop motion and their own focus return. A replace over an open stack runs one level up and leaves the sheets beneath covered. Non-modal sheets (hasScrim={false}) replace each other the same way, with no scrim: they are hosted in the browser top layer as manual popovers, so the entering step orders above the retained one with no page-level z-index, and toasts raised before or while the sheet is open stay above it. Below the Popover API support floor (Tier 2 in the browser support guide) the sheet falls back to show() in page stacking order: usable, but with no promise over later page content. A non-modal sheet returns focus to its opener on close only while focus is still inside it; focus taken elsewhere on the live page stays there. Focus. Opening a sheet, modal or not, focuses its data-autofocus field (a TextInput with hasAutoFocus) in every browser. Without one, focus goes wherever the engine's native dialog focusing steps land: the panel in Chromium, the first focusable control in Firefox. A step entering as a replacement also focuses a data-autofocus descendant first, so a flow that opens on a field keeps the keyboard on it. Closing the top sheet returns focus into the sheet it reveals: to the control that opened it when that control is still there, otherwise to the revealed sheet's panel. When the last sheet closes, the standalone rules apply: finalFocusRef, else the element that opened the sheet, with a focus ring only after keyboard input. When every sheet of a stack closes in one update, focus returns once, to the bottom sheet's finalFocusRef or opener, after the last dialog has closed. Caveats. A Dialog, AlertDialog, or Popover opened from a sheet paints above the sheet and does not make it recede; a sheet opened from inside that Dialog paints above the Dialog and stacks over the sheet beneath. Sheets with hasScrim={false} stay out of the stack entirely (they replace each other, but never stack, recede, or take the scrim). A sheet React hides (a suspended Suspense boundary, Activity mode="hidden") leaves the stack and closes its dialog; when it is shown again it is presented again, on top. Only sheets rendered in the same document stack; a sheet inside an iframe is its own stack. |

| [Drawer](components/Drawer.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Drawer` | [DrawerHeader](components/DrawerHeader.md) | A side panel that floats above page content for inspectors and detail views: the "click a table row, see its details" pattern. Unlike a docked panel it overlays the layout instead of reflowing it. Works on desktop and touch: the width budget applies on desktop and the panel preserves a 56px page reveal below 640px without exceeding the width budget. Escape closes the drawer (unless purpose is required) and focus returns to the element that opened it. Entry/exit slide animation respects prefers-reduced-motion. On a phone or tablet (a coarse primary pointer), a tap or a drag that lands while the drawer is still sliding in reaches nothing (for a drawer without a scrim, only one on the panel: the page stays live), and the drawer finishes sliding in; keys and assistive technology stay live, and a mouse or a trackpad still clicks: at once when it was the last pointer used, otherwise once it moves. Stacking contract: sibling drawers stack last-opened on top, Escape closes only the topmost, and closing peels innermost-first; render them as siblings, never nested. Like Dialog, the drawer is a container: its content area is inset by --spacing-4 (16px) by default, by the padding prop, or by a theme's padding on drawer. Compose the header, body, and footer the way Dialog does, with a Layout: DrawerHeader in the header slot (it shows a close button when you pass it onOpenChange, like DialogHeader), the body in LayoutContent, and actions in LayoutFooter. The Layout redistributes the inset to those regions so they line up on one content line, and the header is not inset twice. A lone Section child also escapes the inset. Drawer renders no close button of its own, so give every drawer a visible way to close, especially a non-modal one, which has no scrim to click. Put data-autofocus on the control that should receive focus on open. Choosing a surface: use Dialog for a centered decision or short form, Drawer for full-height side detail that keeps the page in sight, BottomSheet for block-axis sheets on touch, and a docked panel (a layout column) when content should reflow the page instead of floating over it. Theming: the panel is the single stable target (astryx-drawer, with data-side reflecting side), and the scrim is the panel's native ::backdrop. DrawerHeader exposes astryx-drawer-header targets for its row, slots, and close icon. |

Keyboard typeahead matches a native select: typing on the focused closed trigger selects the matching option directly, repeated presses cycle through options sharing a first letter, and spaces count as match characters ("new y" reaches "New York"). With the menu open, typing moves the highlight and Enter commits. With hasSearch, typing on the closed trigger opens the popup and seeds the search input. |
| [Skeleton](components/Skeleton.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Skeleton` |  | An animated shimmer placeholder that previews the shape of content while it loads. Use it to build loading screens that match the layout of the real content. For content with unknown dimensions, use Spinner instead. |
| [Slider](components/Slider.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Slider` |  | A draggable control for selecting a numeric value or range within defined bounds. Supports single value and range selection, tick marks, custom value formatting, and vertical orientation. Use it when users need to explore a continuous range, such as volume, price, or percentage. Under a finger, on any touch device, it tracks as UISlider does: only the thumb takes a drag, through a target larger than it, the value follows the finger’s travel rather than jumping to it, a release coasts on before `onChangeEnd`, a swipe from the track scrolls the page, and a tap on the track or a mark sets the value when the finger lifts (the thumb springs there). A mouse drag on a thumb tracks the same way, past the same 10 px in any direction, with no lift or coast; a mouse press on the track moves the thumb there, and only a primary click presses. A pen drags as a finger does, claiming only along the track, and its drag ends at the release with no coast. A wheel or a trackpad scroll over the slider goes to whatever scrolls under it. |
| [Spinner](components/Spinner.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Spinner` |  | An animated loading indicator for processes with unknown duration, such as data fetching or form submission. Supports visible labels, multiple sizes, and a dark background variant. For content with known dimensions, use Skeleton instead. |
| [StatusDot](components/StatusDot.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/StatusDot` |  | A small colored dot that communicates status like online/offline presence or severity levels. Supports five semantic variants and an optional pulse animation. Always pair with a visible text label, as color alone should not carry meaning. |
| [Stepper](components/Stepper.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Stepper` | [Step](components/Step.md) | Steppers display progress through a sequence of logical and numbered steps. Use them for multi-step workflows like forms, onboarding flows, or checkout processes where users need to see their position and the steps ahead. Rendered as an ordered list (not a navigation landmark). |
| [Switch](components/Switch.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Switch` |  | A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead. Under a finger it moves like the iOS switch on every touch screen: a press lifts the thumb, a drag across flips it, lifting the finger commits, and a tap toggles through the browser’s click. The thumb keeps its circle and size on every device, and under a coarse pointer the invisible hit area grows toward 44 × 44 px, stopping halfway to any neighbouring control so a tap goes to the nearer one. With reduced motion on, a change cross-fades on a touch screen and is immediate with a mouse. |
| [Table](components/Table.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Table` | [TableBody](components/TableBody.md), [TableCell](components/TableCell.md), [TableFooter](components/TableFooter.md), [TableHeader](components/TableHeader.md), [TableHeaderCell](components/TableHeaderCell.md), [TableRow](components/TableRow.md), [TableSelectionToolbar](components/TableSelectionToolbar.md) | Table displays structured data in rows and columns with consistent dimensionality. It supports rich cell content, sorting, selection, pagination, and column management through a composable plugin system. Use Table for data sets with uniform structure; for simpler or inconsistent data, consider a list or card layout instead. |
| [Tab](components/Tab.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Tab` | [TabList](components/TabList.md), [TabMenu](components/TabMenu.md) | Individual tab item that renders as a button or an anchor link, with selected-state styling and optional icons. |
| [Text](components/Text.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Text` |  | Text renders styled body text and headings from the theme. Use Text with a semantic type for body copy, labels, and captions, and Heading for section titles that output the correct h1–h6 element. |
| [TextArea](components/TextArea.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/TextArea` |  | TextArea is a multi-line text input for collecting longer-form content like comments, descriptions, or messages. Use it when the expected input spans multiple lines. For shorter, single-line values, use TextInput. |
| [TextInput](components/TextInput.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/TextInput` |  | TextInput collects short-form text like names, emails, or search queries. Use it for single-line values where the expected input is brief. Pair it with validation status to guide users through required or formatted fields. |
| [Thumbnail](components/Thumbnail.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Thumbnail` |  | Thumbnail displays a compact, square preview of an image attachment. It shows a shimmer effect while uploading, the image on success, and a placeholder icon when no source is set. Use it in chat composers, file upload lists, or anywhere you need a small image preview with optional remove and click actions. |
| [TimeInput](components/TimeInput.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/TimeInput` |  | TimeInput uses a browser/OS time picker on coarse pointers by default and Astryx's typed field on fine pointers. It converts values to a standard format and supports arrow-key adjustment on the typed surface. Use it in forms, scheduling flows, or any interface where users need to select a specific time. |
| [Timer](components/Timer.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Timer` |  | Displays a standardized elapsed duration for active work without scheduling a React render on every tick. Elapsed format updates by second below one hour and by minute after one hour; clock format remains second-precise. |
| [Timestamp](components/Timestamp.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Timestamp` |  | Timestamp formats a date or time value into human-readable text. Use it to show when something was created, updated, or is scheduled; picking relative for recency, absolute for precision, or auto to let the component decide. |
| [Toast](components/Toast.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Toast` |  | Toast shows a brief, non-blocking notification to confirm an action or present temporary information. Use it for scenarios where the user needs feedback but not a decision, such as saving, deleting, or changing a status. For production use, prefer the `useToast()` hook; it handles positioning, stacking, auto-dismiss, and deduplication via `ToastViewport`. Toasts stay within viewport and safe-area gutters, wrap long message content, and enter, exit, or swipe-dismiss toward their configured top or bottom edge. The vertical swipe uses the same spatial model as placement motion: top Toasts leave upward and bottom Toasts leave downward. Swipe waits for dominant edge-directed intent before cancelling native touch movement and reports the existing manual dismissal reason. Pen is supported as direct-contact input; mouse drag is excluded to avoid conflicting with desktop text selection, where the visible close control remains available. Set `isAutoHide: false` explicitly when an action or message must remain available. The `Toast` component renders the visual toast element inline and is useful for previews, documentation, and static showcases where the viewport lifecycle is not needed. |
| [Token](components/Token.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Token` |  | Token is a small, inline element for representing discrete pieces of associated data, like tags, categories, or selections. Use it to label content, show active filters, or represent removable items like selected recipients in a compose field. |
| [Tokenizer](components/Tokenizer.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Tokenizer` |  | Tokenizer is a multi-select input that lets users search, select, and manage multiple items displayed as removable chips. Use it when users need to build a set of selections from a searchable data source, like adding team members, applying tags, or choosing filters. |
| [Toolbar](components/Toolbar.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Toolbar` |  | Toolbar is a horizontal bar with left, center, and right areas. Use it for contextual actions within a content area (above a table, inside a card, or in a panel), not as a page-level header. Set the size once on the toolbar and all buttons, inputs, and tabs inside it match automatically. |
| [Tooltip](components/Tooltip.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Tooltip` |  | A short text hint that appears on hover or focus, anchored to a trigger element. Use it to describe icon-only buttons, show the full text of truncated labels, or provide supplementary context without cluttering the UI. |
| [TreeList](components/TreeList.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/TreeList` |  | An expandable tree structure for displaying hierarchical data with branch connector lines. Use it for file explorers, nested category browsers, or any interface that visualizes parent-child relationships. Under a finger, expanding a row glides the rows below it while its children fade in on the same timing, and a collapse plays it back; pass an `animatedLayout` handle for content after the tree to glide too. |
| [Typeahead](components/Typeahead.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/Typeahead` | [BaseTypeahead](components/BaseTypeahead.md), [TypeaheadItem](components/TypeaheadItem.md) | A searchable input for selecting a single item from a large or dynamic dataset. Results appear as the user types, with support for async data sources, debounced search, and custom item rendering. Use it when the option list is too large for a Selector dropdown. |
| [InternationalizationProvider](components/InternationalizationProvider.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/InternationalizationProvider` | [LinkProvider](components/LinkProvider.md), [MediaTheme](components/MediaTheme.md), [Theme](components/Theme.md) | Wraps your app to set the active locale and (optionally) merge additional translation catalogs + per-locale overrides. Astryx components inside the subtree resolve their strings against this context. If no provider is present, components fall back to the shipped English defaults. |
| [VisuallyHidden](components/VisuallyHidden.md) | `@astryxdesign/core/VisuallyHidden` |  | Renders content in the accessibility tree while hiding it visually. Use for accessible names on icon-only controls, aria-live announcement regions, and supplementary screen-reader context. Deliberately has no styling props; the whole point is to stay invisible. `xstyle` is still accepted and ignored, only so code written against 0.7.2 keeps compiling; a planned minor removes it. |

## Hooks (78)

- [useAnnounce](hooks/useAnnounce.md): Imperatively announces a message to screen readers through a visually-hidden live region. Use it for state that is only conveyed visually; search result counts, "no results", loading and saved confirmations, validation errors (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages). The polite and assertive regions are created empty on first use and stay mounted, which is what makes announcements reliable: most screen readers ignore a live region that is inserted together with its content. Each message is cleared a couple of seconds after it is announced so stale status does not linger in the accessibility tree. A message is delivered where its caller is: from inside an open Astryx modal it goes to a region inside that modal and is heard there with no change to the calling code; a message sent just as the modal is dismissed is delivered through whatever is exposed afterwards rather than lost. A call made outside the modal, even by the component that renders it, uses the page-body region.
- [useCombobox](hooks/useCombobox.md): Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an “add people” field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.
- [useFocusTrap](hooks/useFocusTrap.md): Traps focus within a container element following the WAI-ARIA dialog focus trap pattern. Listens to focus events on the document and redirects focus back into the container if a Tab from inside it moves focus out. Handles both Tab and Shift+Tab wrapping. A Tab pressed while focus is outside the container is left to the page, so an open non-modal surface never takes over the focus order of the page. When the trap deactivates or unmounts, focus is restored to the element that was focused before activation, unless focus was already moved elsewhere or never entered the trap (so popups that keep focus on their trigger, like comboboxes, are unaffected). Mouse clicks outside the container are not intercepted; use a light-dismiss handler for that.
- [useGridFocus](hooks/useGridFocus.md): Manages keyboard navigation within a 2D grid following the WAI-ARIA grid pattern. Supports arrow keys for cell-to-cell navigation, Home/End for row boundaries, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End for grid boundaries, and Page Up/Down for custom callbacks (e.g., month navigation in calendars). Boundary navigation callbacks allow cross-grid navigation.
- [useIndicatorFocusRing](hooks/useIndicatorFocusRing.md): Draws the standard focus ring on the indicator of a control whose real input is visually hidden; a checkbox or radio focuses an opacity-0 input, so the ring has to appear on the picture beside it. The ring is painted imperatively on the indicator's own element, which is the only element whose border-radius can shape it, and only on :focus-visible, so pointer clicks stay quiet. Owning it here means a theme-supplied indicator cannot ship a control with no visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) by ignoring a prop.
- [useKeyboardHint](hooks/useKeyboardHint.md): Shows an ephemeral "← → to navigate" hint anchored to the focused item the first time a roving-tabindex composite (Toolbar, TabList, SegmentedControl, etc.) receives keyboard focus. It teaches sighted keyboard users that arrow keys move within the group. The hint renders arrow keys with Kbd in the top layer (popover="manual") and is CSS-anchor-positioned to the focused element, so overflow containers never clip it. It auto-dismisses on the first arrow press, on timeout, or on blur, and does not re-show for that instance. Toolbar, TabList, and SegmentedControl wire this in automatically; reach for the hook directly only when building a custom roving-tabindex widget.
- [useListFocus](hooks/useListFocus.md): Manages keyboard navigation within a linear list following WAI-ARIA menu/listbox/toolbar patterns. Supports arrow key navigation (vertical, horizontal, or both), Home/End for boundaries, optional wrap-around, RTL, and Escape to close. Opt into hasRovingTabIndex for composite widgets (toolbars, segmented controls, tab strips) that own a single tab stop. Suitable for dropdown menus, toolbars, and any 1D focusable list.
- [useMultiCombobox](hooks/useMultiCombobox.md): Tracks the active option of a multi-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers MultiSelector; unlike useCombobox, toggling an option keeps the list open, and rows can carry an action cell. It renders nothing and sets no attributes: the caller renders the control and the list, and wires the ARIA attributes from what it returns.
- [useTreeFocus](hooks/useTreeFocus.md): Manages roving-tabindex focus and the WAI-ARIA tree keyboard model. ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End roam linearly over the visible treeitems (skipping disabled ones), while ArrowRight/ArrowLeft carry tree semantics (expand/collapse, move to first-child/parent). Enter/Space activate, and printable characters trigger typeahead.
- [useTypeahead](hooks/useTypeahead.md): Adds APG type-to-focus search to a collection: printable keystrokes are buffered (resetting after a pause), and the first item whose label starts with the buffer (ignoring case, accents, the stroked letters đ ł ø ħ ŧ ƀ and Turkish ı/İ, the same in every locale; a typed accent prefers the exact match) is reported through onMatch. Pressing the same letter repeatedly cycles through the matches rather than filtering deeper. It moves nothing itself; pair it with the collection's own focus management, most often useListFocus or useGridFocus.
- [createReorderable](hooks/createReorderable.md): Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.
- [useClickableContainer](hooks/useClickableContainer.md): Makes a container element clickable while preserving nested interactive element behavior. Solves the "nested interactive elements" problem: when a card is clickable but contains buttons/links, clicking those should NOT trigger the card's action. Detects interactive ancestors between the click target and the container, and ignores text selections. Supports href navigation (including middle-click and Ctrl/Cmd+click for new tabs).
- [useClipboard](hooks/useClipboard.md): Copy-to-clipboard behavior: the clipboard write, a transient isCopied flag with its own reset timer, and an optional polite screen-reader announcement. Extracted so every copy affordance is a thin control over one implementation instead of re-deriving the timer and announcement. Rapid re-copies restart the reset timer so the confirmation always lasts the full duration, and the timer is cleaned up on unmount. CodeBlock and Timestamp build their built-in copy buttons on it; reach for it directly when building a copy affordance that is not a plain icon button (a menu item, a labeled text button, a copy-on-click value chip).
- [useCollapsible](hooks/useCollapsible.md): Reusable hook that encapsulates the collapsible state machine. Supports three modes: group-controlled (inside CollapsibleGroup), controlled (isOpen + onOpenChange), and uncontrolled (self-managed with defaultIsOpen). Used internally by Card and Section.
- [useContainerReveal](hooks/useContainerReveal.md): A headless hover/focus reveal primitive. Gives a container a scoped trigger that reveals (or conceals) content inside it when the container is hovered or receives keyboard focus: the classic "row actions appear on hover" pattern. The reveal is CSS-only: no hover state lives in React and hovering never triggers a re-render. The caller authors no StyleX for the reveal itself; the hook hands out the container and content styles, and a nested container shadows its ancestor, so nested containers never leak hover/focus into one another. Accessible by construction: revealed content is visually hidden at rest with position and opacity (never display:none), so it stays mounted, keeps its place in the tab order, and is announced to assistive technology; it reveals on :focus-within so keyboard users see it when tabbing in, stays visible on touch (never gated behind hover on coarse pointers), and honors prefers-reduced-motion.
- [useDragToSnapPoints](hooks/useDragToSnapPoints.md): Lets a drag move an element along one axis and settles it on snap points when the finger lifts, the way an iOS sheet settles on its detents: on the nearest snap point to where it is, on the next one in its direction after a quick flick, and back where it started when the finger was moving back. The settle continues the release's velocity. For a bottom sheet, use BottomSheet's `snapPoints`; for a scrolling row, Carousel's `hasSnap`. Outside React, use `createDragToSnapPoints`.
- [useHotkeys](hooks/useHotkeys.md): Registers global keyboard shortcuts with a single window keydown listener per hook instance. Handlers live in a ref, so re-renders never re-subscribe. Skips events from typing targets (input, textarea, select, contenteditable) unless allowInInputs, skips defaultPrevented events, and calls preventDefault() on match. SSR-safe.
- [useHoverCard](hooks/useHoverCard.md): Headless hook for hover-triggered floating cards. Builds on useLayer with hover/focus intent detection, configurable delays, safe hover behavior, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for rich previews on hover when you need full control over the trigger or rendered content.
- [useInputContainer](hooks/useInputContainer.md): Makes an input container wrapper clickable, delegating focus to the inner input/textarea when the user clicks non-interactive areas (icons, padding, status indicators). Built on top of useClickableContainer, so nested interactive elements (clear buttons, calendar toggles, links) are handled safely; clicking them does NOT steal focus from the input. Automatically detects input type: text-like inputs receive .focus(), while other types (checkbox, radio, file) receive .click().
- [useInputStatusIcon](hooks/useInputStatusIcon.md): Builds the on-field status affordance for a bordered input and its accessibility wiring, so every input in the family behaves the same for a given status. The attached variant renders a plain glyph and leaves the text to the message box; the detached variant renders nothing here, because the message box already carries its own icon; the tooltip variant renders a real focusable button whose tooltip is reachable by keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive tech. Use it when building a bordered input, not for field-level messaging.
- [useInteractiveRole](hooks/useInteractiveRole.md): Resolves what a polymorphic component should render as, in one place: href wins, then onClick, then an interactive trigger context supplied by a parent (Popover, DropdownMenu and friends), then inert. Use it in any component that is sometimes a link, sometimes a button, and sometimes plain content; Token, Thumbnail, Item and ClickableCard all do. Because context is part of the resolution, a component built on it becomes a valid trigger for new surfaces without changing.
- [useLayer](hooks/useLayer.md): Core positioning hook for rendering overlay content using CSS Anchor Positioning and the Popover API. Use it as the foundation for custom popovers, hover cards, tooltips, and fixed-position layers when higher-level components are not enough. Both modes use theme body text defaults and end ancestor surface/group membership as a whole, including group-owned state. Explicit props and unrelated contexts remain unchanged. Apply intentional formatting through render styles or content, and establish complete content-local providers inside the rendered layer.
- [useLightbox](hooks/useLightbox.md): State management and accessible trigger wiring for Lightbox. Eliminates boilerplate for managing open state and current index. Returns trigger props with button role, tabIndex={0}, aria-haspopup="dialog", and keyboard activation handlers, along with a pre-wired Lightbox element that handles dismissal, next/previous navigation, and focus restoration.
- [useLongPress](hooks/useLongPress.md): Detects a single-finger press-and-hold and reports where it happened, so touch users can reach affordances that a pointer gets from right-click. iOS Safari never synthesizes a contextmenu event on long-press, which makes this the only touch route into a cursor-positioned surface such as ContextMenu. The press cancels on movement, lift, multi-touch or unmount. The hold is timed on the touch events’ own timestamps: when a busy page handles the lift late, a finger held for the full delay still reports its long press, before the lift acts.
- [useMenuPress](hooks/useMenuPress.md): The press model of macOS and iOS menus, for any pointer: the row under the pointer when it is RELEASED is the row that acts, the highlight follows the pointer while it is held, a mouse opens the menu on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger held on the trigger opens it with the finger still down. The pointer is tracked at document level by pointerId, so a finger that slid off the row it landed on is still followed; the click the browser reports at the end of a touch, aimed at the row where the touch began, is swallowed so nothing acts twice. DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, DropdownMenuSubMenu, Selector and the menu bottom sheet already mount it; reach for it directly only when building a menu-like surface of your own.
- [useOverlay](hooks/useOverlay.md): Adds overlay behavior to a container you already render, such as a Card or a custom media frame, without the wrapper Overlay adds. Spread containerRef and containerProps on the container, then render element (or renderOverlay(children)) once inside it. The scrim is absolutely positioned, so it covers the nearest positioned ancestor: the container itself, or a positioned section inside it such as an image area. Visibility is CSS-driven from the container's :hover and :focus-within, so with showOn 'hover' a keyboard user reveals the content by moving focus into the container. Hidden content is not focusable, so the container needs a focusable element before the overlay content in tab order. A revealed scrim takes pointer input over the area it covers, so put that element outside the scrim, or use a top or bottom strip and keep it in the part the strip leaves uncovered.
- [usePopover](hooks/usePopover.md): Headless hook for click-triggered popovers with focus trapping. Combines useLayer with useFocusTrap, auto-focus, light dismiss, Escape handling, and an optional hidden close button for accessible dialog-like popover behavior. Every painted surface emits the canonical popover target. A custom composition needing a distinct stable seam should pass and document its own surfaceTarget.
- [useToast](hooks/useToast.md): Hook for showing toast notifications from anywhere in your component tree. Returns a function that accepts toast options and shows the notification. Works automatically with LayerProvider or self-mounts a fallback viewport.
- [useTooltip](hooks/useTooltip.md): Headless hook for hover/focus-triggered tooltips. Builds on useLayer with hover intent, keyboard focus handling, and accessible aria-describedby linking. Use for custom trigger elements that need tooltip behavior without the wrapper component.
- [useAppShellMobile](hooks/useAppShellMobile.md): Hook for reading and controlling AppShell mobile navigation state from descendants of AppShell. Use it for custom mobile nav triggers, closing the drawer after route changes, or coordinating AppShell-adjacent mobile experiences with the same breakpoint used by mobile nav.
- [useOverflow](hooks/useOverflow.md): Measures children rendered in a hidden container to determine how many fit in the available width without flickering. Uses ResizeObserver to react to container and measured-child size changes. The measurement container should hold all items plus an optional overflow indicator element (identified by a data-overflow-indicator attribute).
- [useResizable](hooks/useResizable.md): Hook for adding drag-to-resize behavior to layout regions. Supports single-region and multi-region configurations with snap points, collapsible panels, localStorage persistence, and cascade resize ordering.
- [useScrollLock](hooks/useScrollLock.md): Locks page scroll while active and keeps the page where it is. The page gets overflow: hidden (on the root, or on body when its own overflow is the one the viewport uses), which stops wheel, keyboard and scrollbar scrolling, and overscroll-behavior-y: none on the root and body, which stops the overscroll bounce while the lock holds. Where the primary pointer is coarse (phones and tablets), a one-finger pan that would scroll the page is cancelled, because iOS Safari scrolls an overflow: hidden page under a finger; pans that a scroller inside the overlay can take, drags on a native range input, pinch-zoom, and one-finger drags on a pinch-zoomed page (which pan the zoomed view) still work. The scroll offset never changes, so nothing jumps when the lock starts or ends, and iOS Safari keeps its toolbar as it was. Where the hidden scrollbar takes layout space (desktop), the hook holds its gutter open with scrollbar-gutter: stable, so the page, including any position: fixed chrome, does not shift sideways.
- [useScrollOverflow](hooks/useScrollOverflow.md): Tracks scroll overflow state for a horizontally scrollable container. Returns a ref callback and state booleans that update as the user scrolls, the container resizes, or its content changes (a child added, removed or resized, or a new gap or padding). Uses scroll event listeners, ResizeObserver and MutationObserver for reactive updates. Tolerance of 1px is applied to avoid sub-pixel false positives.
- [useScrollableArea](hooks/useScrollableArea.md): Adds canonical axis-aware scroll behavior to structure owned by the caller. An axis is effective only when its computed overflow is scroll-capable and geometry exceeds the shared 1px tolerance. Both viewport and content boxes are observed.
- [useLinkify](hooks/useLinkify.md): Finds URLs, email addresses and custom patterns in plain text and returns React nodes with a Link for each match; the links respect LinkProvider for client-side routing. Use it wherever user- or tool-authored plain text should grow safe, styled links without pre-parsing it into markup: activity feeds, comment threads, description fields. Custom patterns turn project-specific references (issue numbers like #123, ticket IDs) into links by supplying a regex plus an href builder — e.g. an issue tracker pattern that maps captures onto its URL scheme. When matches overlap, the earliest one wins, and at the same start a custom pattern wins over the built-in ones, so a custom #123 pattern coexists with URL detection in the same string.
- [useImageMode](hooks/useImageMode.md): Detects whether an image is predominantly dark or light by sampling pixels via OffscreenCanvas. Uses APCA perceptual lightness (sRGB linearization + power curve) for accurate detection, especially on saturated colors. Runs entirely off the paint path: no visible canvas, no layout thrash. Supports regional sampling for detecting luminance where text overlays will appear. Returns null while loading and falls back gracefully on CORS or network errors.
- [useMediaQuery](hooks/useMediaQuery.md): SSR-safe media query hook that subscribes to window.matchMedia changes. Returns whether the given media query matches. Always returns false on first render for SSR compatibility. Where `window.matchMedia` is missing, it returns its server default and never throws.
- [useAnimatedLayout](hooks/useAnimatedLayout.md): Returns a handle to pass to a component whose size changes, such as TreeList or Collapsible. When that component changes size, it and the content after it inside `containerRef` animate together on one shared motion role. Fixed and stuck sticky elements stay put, the glide never scrolls the area, and Reduce Motion is respected. It applies under every pointer, a mouse included. Without the handle a component keeps its jump: content after it takes its place at once. Content after the change may mix Astryx components and your own elements; none of it opts in.
- [useAnimator](hooks/useAnimator.md): Animates one element with the motion Astryx's own components use. Call `animator.animate` to spring an element to new values on the state-change motion, `animator.decay` to fling it with the momentum of a released scroll view, and `animator.set` to move it directly, so a card can follow a finger, snap back and be thrown away. To animate an area's layout as its items change, use `useAnimatedLayout`; for what a component already animates, such as a sheet's detents or a carousel's snapping, use the component's own props. Outside React, use `createAnimator`.
- [useEntryAnimation](hooks/useEntryAnimation.md): Returns a StyleX style for animating an element on mount. Only animates when the element is dynamically inserted after the initial page paint; elements rendered on page load are not animated. Uses Astryx motion tokens (duration, easing) for consistent animation timing. Server-rendered elements hydrate without the entry style and never animate; elements mounted after hydration animate.
- [usePanGesture](hooks/usePanGesture.md): Reports a drag on an element as values, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit’s 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap, and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. With `axis`, a scroll across that axis that starts on the element stays the page’s; without it, the pan takes a drag in any direction, so a finger’s scroll that starts on the element moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page. The hook is a thin layer over `createPanGesture`, the same API for code without React. A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons or arrow keys (WCAG 2.5.7). The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: honor the user’s reduced-motion setting in the animation that moves the element. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet’s `snapPoints`, Carousel’s `hasSnap`.
- [usePressFeedback](hooks/usePressFeedback.md): The touch press model every Astryx pressable uses, for a local component that paints its own press. Under a finger, CSS `:active` paints on the touch itself and can outlive the start of a scroll; the press model instead tracks the touch the way UIKit tracks a control: it highlights as the finger lands (after the content-touch delay inside a scroller, where a flick paints nothing), a quick tap answers at the lift, and a scroll that takes the touch cancels it with no fade. One document-level controller does this for every marked element (installed by the first pressable to mount, removed by the last to unmount), so calling the hook adds no listener or state to your element. On a desktop a mouse press is still your `:active` rule: keep it, and drop it under `@media (pointer: coarse)` the way the built-in components do. That query reads the primary pointer, so on a phone or tablet it also drops `:active` for a connected mouse, trackpad or keyboard; the controller paints those presses there (at once, faded at the release), so nothing goes unanswered.
- [useSnapPaging](hooks/useSnapPaging.md): Gives a Carousel iOS paging on native snap's stops: pass the value as hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}. Under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, a flick moves one view, or one item with {pages: 'item'}, and the row rests on an item's start edge. A mouse wheel keeps native snapping. Only a carousel given the value loads the paging code.
- [useOutlineFromMarkdown](hooks/useOutlineFromMarkdown.md): Extracts the headings of a Markdown string for an Outline next to the rendered document. It uses the parser and heading slugs that Markdown uses, so in a complete document each item links to its heading, and fenced code never counts as a heading. The result is memoized on the source and the options. Outside React, use parseOutlineFromMarkdown.
- [useStreamingText](hooks/useStreamingText.md): Smooths bursty streamed text into a steady character-by-character reveal using requestAnimationFrame. Decouples arrival rate from display rate. Advances on word and syntax boundaries to avoid slicing mid-markdown or mid-word, preventing visual glitches with markdown renderers. Animation timing derives from Astryx motion tokens via useTheme when available, with sensible fallbacks outside a theme provider. Snaps to full text when isStreaming becomes false.
- [useCalendarConstraints](hooks/useCalendarConstraints.md): Provides date constraint validation for calendar views and custom range pickers. It combines boundary dates, span limits measured from an in-progress range start, and custom rules (such as weekly closures or blackout dates) into an isDateDisabled predicate. Calendar uses it internally to disable day buttons; use it directly when building bespoke scheduling interfaces or range pickers.
- [useCalendarDays](hooks/useCalendarDays.md): Builds the day grid for one month: every date to show, including the previous and next months' days that fill the first and last weeks, grouped into weeks, plus localized weekday header names that start on weekStartsOn. It is the layout Calendar uses, for a custom month view such as a compact availability grid or a mini calendar. It returns data only: rendering, selection, keyboard navigation and the grid's accessibility semantics are the caller's.
- [useCalendarNavigation](hooks/useCalendarNavigation.md): Manages visible month state and pagination for calendar components. It provides previous/next month stepping, localized month-year header strings, and pending focus tracking so keyboard arrow navigation seamlessly moves focus across month boundaries into the adjacent month. Use it directly when composing custom calendar headers, pager controls, or dual-month availability pickers.
- [useCollator](hooks/useCollator.md): Returns the sanctioned locale-aware comparator for custom sorting. The collator is recreated when the provider locale or an option changes.
- [useIcon](hooks/useIcon.md): Resolves a semantic icon name to a React node through the nearest Theme, so a custom component draws the same success, warning or error icon that Astryx components draw and follows a theme that overrides it. Resolution reads the nearest Theme's icons (outside any Theme, the registered theme the document root names), then registerIcons() overrides, then the built-in default. The node is returned as is, with no size or color wrapper: the built-in icons are 1em squares in currentColor, so they follow the surrounding text. A function entry is read at {size: 'md'}. Render <Icon icon={name} /> instead when the icon needs another size, a color or a label.
- [useLinkComponent](hooks/useLinkComponent.md): Resolves which component renders a link, so a custom component's links follow the app's router the same way Astryx's own links do. The order is the as argument, then the nearest LinkProvider's component, then a native anchor. Render the returned component with href (and to, for a router that reads it). Before rendering it checks both destinations under the Link href rule: a rejected destination renders an anchor with no destination, and a custom router is never invoked with it. A custom component receives to={href} unless to is passed explicitly.
- [useLocale](hooks/useLocale.md): Reads the authoritative Astryx locale. Use it to thread the provider locale into pure formatting helpers and sibling-package APIs; do not derive a second locale from navigator.language or a hardcoded literal.
- [usePowerSearchConfig](hooks/usePowerSearchConfig.md): Memoizes a PowerSearch configuration built from typed field definitions and returns it along with an applyFilters function for client-side filtering. Automatically maps field types (string, number, boolean, date, enum, etc.) to their canonical operators and provides an efficient predicate evaluator to filter datasets.
- [useTableColumnSettingsState](hooks/useTableColumnSettingsState.md): Headless column visibility and ordering state management for Table. Manages which columns are active, provides toggle and reset operations, and produces a config object that feeds directly into useTableColumnSettings. Renderer-agnostic and pairs with any column picker UI.
- [useTableSortableState](hooks/useTableSortableState.md): Owns a Table's sort state and sorts the rows locally, as a convenience layer over useTableSortable. Pass the rows in, render sortedData, and hand sortConfig to useTableSortable. The hook keeps the state (or reads it from sort and onSortChange when controlled), so header clicks re-sort the rows with no sort code in the component. With isMultiSortEnabled, Shift+click adds tiebreaker columns. For data sorted on a server, use useTableSortable directly and sort where the data lives.
- [useTranslator](hooks/useTranslator.md): Returns a translator function that resolves keys against the current locale, provider overrides, and the shipped English fallback catalog. Call inside a component; the returned function can be used anywhere within that component's scope.
- [useDevWarning](hooks/useDevWarning.md): Fires a dev-only "Component: message" console warning once per mount while the condition holds. It is the render-safe way for a component to flag misuse: warning straight from the render body repeats on every render, and gating it with state adds a re-render, so this uses a ref and an effect instead. For a warning outside a component, use the imperative devWarn utility.
- [useMergedRefs](hooks/useMergedRefs.md): Combines multiple object or callback refs into one stable callback ref. Use it when a component must forward a consumer ref while also attaching internal refs. Unlike calling mergeRefs during render, the callback identity stays stable across unrelated rerenders, so React does not detach and reattach the element.
- [useTheme](hooks/useTheme.md): Programmatic access to theme tokens for non-CSS consumers like SVG, canvas, Vega, D3, maps, or chart libraries that need values in JavaScript instead of CSS custom property references.

## Page templates (776)

- [AI Chat Conversation](templates/ai-chat.md) (`ai-chat`): Transcript of alternating turns carrying mixed rich content inline (markdown, code blocks, collapsible tool-call output) beside a resizable artifact panel that holds generated output while the stream keeps scrolling.
- [AI Chat Landing](templates/ai-chat-landing.md) (`ai-chat-landing`): Zero-state entry surface centered on a single composer with suggestion chips instead of history, sized for the moment before any content exists. The empty counterpart to a transcript.
- [AlertDialog — Delete](templates/AlertDialogDeleteConfirmation.md) (`AlertDialogDeleteConfirmation`): A delete button that asks the user to confirm before deleting.
- [AlertDialog — Loading](templates/AlertDialogAsyncAction.md) (`AlertDialogAsyncAction`): A confirmation dialog that shows a spinner while the action runs.
- [Analytics Dashboard](templates/dashboard.md) (`dashboard`): Three-band analytics: a row of headline tiles, then charts, then supporting tables, all re-reading from one global filter bar. Breadth over depth, a summary surface rather than a drill-down.
- [AppShell](templates/AppShellShowcase.md) (`AppShellShowcase`): A basic app shell with content padding.
- [AppShell — Content Only](templates/AppShellContentOnly.md) (`AppShellContentOnly`): Minimal shell with no navigation, useful for full-bleed pages, auth screens, or embedded views.
- [AppShell — Side Nav Only](templates/AppShellSideNavOnly.md) (`AppShellSideNavOnly`): App shell with SideNav header providing app identity, no TopNav needed.
- [AppShell — Top Nav Only](templates/AppShellTopNavOnly.md) (`AppShellTopNavOnly`): Simple layout with TopNav and no side navigation, suitable for landing pages.
- [AppShell — Top Nav with Side Nav](templates/AppShellTopNavWithSideNav.md) (`AppShellTopNavWithSideNav`): The most common layout with TopNav for app identity and SideNav for page-level navigation.
- [AppShell — With Banner](templates/AppShellWithBanner.md) (`AppShellWithBanner`): Full layout with TopNav, SideNav, and a dismissable info banner between the nav and content.
- [AspectRatio](templates/AspectRatioShowcase.md) (`AspectRatioShowcase`): Three aspect ratio containers at equal height (1:1, 4:3, and 16:9), each showing an image with its ratio labeled below.
- [AspectRatio — 16:9 Widescreen Image](templates/AspectRatioWidescreen.md) (`AspectRatioWidescreen`): 16:9 widescreen aspect ratio wrapping an image.
- [AspectRatio — Circle Image](templates/AspectRatioCircleImage.md) (`AspectRatioCircleImage`): Circular container via shape="ellipse" with ratio={1}, ideal for avatars and profile images.
- [AspectRatio — Image Gallery](templates/AspectRatioImageGallery.md) (`AspectRatioImageGallery`): Grid of images with consistent 4:3 aspect ratios.
- [AspectRatio — Loading Skeleton](templates/AspectRatioWithSkeleton.md) (`AspectRatioWithSkeleton`): Aspect ratio container with a skeleton loading placeholder.
- [AspectRatio — Square Image](templates/AspectRatioSquareImage.md) (`AspectRatioSquareImage`): 1:1 square aspect ratio, ideal for avatars and Instagram-style images.
- [Avatar](templates/AvatarShowcase.md) (`AvatarShowcase`): Avatars at every size with an image, initials fallback, and a status dot. A quick visual reference for choosing the right size.
- [Avatar — Fallback Chain](templates/AvatarFallbackChain.md) (`AvatarFallbackChain`): Demonstrates the avatar fallback chain: primary image, fallback image, initials, then default icon.
- [Avatar — Group](templates/AvatarGroup.md) (`AvatarGroup`): Overlap multiple avatars in a row to represent a group of people. Use for team lists, PR reviewers, or participant counts where you want to show faces without taking up much space.
- [Avatar — Initials](templates/AvatarInitialsFallback.md) (`AvatarInitialsFallback`): Show initials instead of a photo. The avatar extracts the first and last initials from the name automatically. Use when you only have a user name, like in anonymous accounts or new user onboarding.
- [Avatar — Interactive](templates/AvatarInteractive.md) (`AvatarInteractive`): Make an avatar interactive by passing `href` to render it as a link or `onClick` to render it as a button. Both forms are focusable and show a focus-visible ring for keyboard users. Use for profile links, mention pop-ups, or any avatar people can act on.
- [Avatar — Photo](templates/AvatarWithImage.md) (`AvatarWithImage`): Show a profile photo at different sizes. Use when you have a user photo URL. If the image fails to load, initials are shown instead.
- [Avatar — Status Dot](templates/AvatarWithStatus.md) (`AvatarWithStatus`): Add a status dot to an avatar to show whether someone is online, away, or busy. Use in chat, messaging, or any UI where knowing availability matters.
- [Avatar — Tooltip](templates/AvatarTooltip.md) (`AvatarTooltip`): By default an avatar shows its name in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. Pass a string to show custom text instead, or false to turn the tooltip off.
- [Avatar — User Card](templates/AvatarUserCard.md) (`AvatarUserCard`): Place an avatar next to a name and role to create a user card row. Use for comment headers, contact lists, profile sections, or anywhere you need to identify a person at a glance.
- [AvatarGroup](templates/AvatarGroupShowcase.md) (`AvatarGroupShowcase`): Overlapping avatar rows with a sliced visible set and a server-side overflow count. Shows team members in a compact facepile layout.
- [AvatarGroup — Interactive](templates/AvatarGroupInteractive.md) (`AvatarGroupInteractive`): A facepile whose avatars link to profiles, with an overflow indicator that opens the full member list. The whole group is one Tab stop; arrow keys move between the avatars and the overflow button.
- [AvatarGroupOverflow](templates/AvatarGroupOverflowShowcase.md) (`AvatarGroupOverflowShowcase`): Overflow indicators for hidden avatars, including the default +N label and custom count text.
- [AvatarGroupOverflow — Custom Text](templates/AvatarGroupOverflowCustomText.md) (`AvatarGroupOverflowCustomText`): Provide short custom children such as 12+ when the overflow count needs compact product-specific formatting.
- [AvatarGroupOverflow — Default Count](templates/AvatarGroupOverflowDefault.md) (`AvatarGroupOverflowDefault`): Use AvatarGroupOverflow without children to render the standard +N overflow count.
- [AvatarStatusDot](templates/AvatarStatusDotShowcase.md) (`AvatarStatusDotShowcase`): AvatarStatusDot renders a presence indicator on an Avatar, with variants for positive, neutral, and negative states. The dot size automatically coordinates with the Avatar size.
- [AvatarStatusDot — Variants](templates/AvatarStatusDotVariants.md) (`AvatarStatusDotVariants`): Presence dots on Avatars using the success, neutral, and error variants. Pass an AvatarStatusDot to the Avatar status prop; the dot sizes itself to match the Avatar.
- [Badge — Colors](templates/BadgeCategoryTags.md) (`BadgeCategoryTags`): Tag items with color-coded categories like teams, priorities, or topics. Use the 9 non-semantic color variants when you need to distinguish groups visually.
- [Badge — Counts](templates/BadgeCountBadges.md) (`BadgeCountBadges`): Show a number inside a badge for notification counts, unread messages, or task totals. Use next to icons, nav items, or list labels.
- [Badge — Status](templates/BadgeStatusLabels.md) (`BadgeStatusLabels`): Show the state of an item like Active, Pending, or Failed. Use in table rows, list items, or detail pages where users need to see status at a glance.
- [Badge — Variants](templates/BadgeShowcase.md) (`BadgeShowcase`): All semantic and color badge variants in a single view. Use semantic variants for status and color variants for categories.
- [Banner — Action](templates/BannerWithActionButton.md) (`BannerWithActionButton`): Add a button to a banner so the user can act on the message. Use for trial expirations, payment failures, or anything that needs a response.
- [Banner — Collapsible](templates/BannerCollapsibleContent.md) (`BannerCollapsibleContent`): Combine an action button, dismiss control, and a collapsible detail area in one banner. Children sit behind the toggle by default; `collapsible={{defaultIsOpen: true}}` starts it open, and `collapsible={false}` drops the toggle entirely. Use for complex notifications like config changes or deployment summaries.
- [Banner — Dismiss](templates/BannerDismissable.md) (`BannerDismissable`): Let the user close a banner after reading it. Use for maintenance notices, feature tips, or any non-critical message the user can acknowledge.
- [Banner — Floating](templates/BannerFloating.md) (`BannerFloating`): A floating banner raised with `elevation="med"`. Banners are inline by default; raise one when it should read as an overlay above content.
- [Banner — Full Width](templates/BannerSectionVariant.md) (`BannerSectionVariant`): A full-width banner with no border radius for page-level notifications. Use at the top of a page for site-wide announcements or maintenance alerts.
- [Banner — Statuses](templates/BannerShowcase.md) (`BannerShowcase`): All four status banners stacked: info, success, warning, and error. A quick visual reference for choosing the right status.
- [Banner — Statuses](templates/BannerStatuses.md) (`BannerStatuses`): All 4 banner statuses: info, success, warning, and error. Use to show persistent messages like updates, confirmations, cautions, or problems at the top of a page or section.
- [BaseTypeahead](templates/BaseTypeaheadShowcase.md) (`BaseTypeaheadShowcase`): A custom result renderer that adds supporting metadata while BaseTypeahead retains option semantics and keyboard behavior.
- [BaseTypeahead — Custom Search Bar](templates/BaseTypeaheadCustomSearch.md) (`BaseTypeaheadCustomSearch`): BaseTypeahead embedded inside a custom-styled wrapper. The wrapper provides its own border and icon chrome; anchorRef positions the dropdown relative to it. Use this pattern when Typeahead's built-in field layout does not fit your composition.
- [Basic](templates/DrawerShowcase.md) (`DrawerShowcase`): Open a modal drawer from a single trigger. The scrim dims the page; Escape, a scrim click, or the header close button closes it, and focus returns to the trigger.
- [Basic Login](templates/login.md) (`login`): Minimal centered credential form on a plain ground: two fields and a submit, nothing competing for attention. The least-chrome entry surface.
- [Blank](templates/blank.md) (`blank`): Bare scaffold: one heading slot, one empty content region, no navigation and no chrome. The starting point when every other layout imposes more structure than wanted.
- [Blockquote — Showcase](templates/BlockquoteShowcase.md) (`BlockquoteShowcase`): Blockquote with and without citation. A quick visual reference for the blockquote component.
- [Blockquote — Testimonials](templates/BlockquoteTestimonials.md) (`BlockquoteTestimonials`): Multiple quotes arranged in a card grid for a testimonials section. Combine with Card and Grid to create social-proof layouts.
- [Blockquote — With Attribution](templates/BlockquoteWithCite.md) (`BlockquoteWithCite`): A plain quote and a quote with a cite attribution. Use cite to credit the original author or source.
- [Bottom Sheet](templates/BottomSheetShowcase.md) (`BottomSheetShowcase`): A mobile filter surface that rises from the bottom edge.
- [Bottom Sheet — Height variants](templates/BottomSheetHeights.md) (`BottomSheetHeights`): Compares hug, capped, and tall starting heights for different amounts of content.
- [Bottom Sheet — Mobile keyboard](templates/BottomSheetMobileKeyboard.md) (`BottomSheetMobileKeyboard`): Uses a tall, scrollable form that keeps focused controls visible above the mobile keyboard.
- [Bottom Sheet — Multi-step flow](templates/BottomSheetSwitcherShowcase.md) (`BottomSheetSwitcherShowcase`): A three-step flow of standalone sheets of different heights, driven by one state value: moving on replaces the open step in place. This is the replacement for the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher.
- [Bottom Sheet — No scrim](templates/BottomSheetNoScrim.md) (`BottomSheetNoScrim`): Keeps the page visible and interactive behind a non-modal bottom sheet.
- [Bottom Sheet — Review flow](templates/BottomSheetSwitcherReviewFlow.md) (`BottomSheetSwitcherReviewFlow`): A two-step form flow of two standalone sheets driven by one state value: Continue replaces the review step with the confirmation in place, and Back returns.
- [Bottom Sheet — Snap points](templates/BottomSheetSnapPoints.md) (`BottomSheetSnapPoints`): Drag-to-resize stops: a half-height working surface, and a peek that slides away and thins the scrim.
- [BreadcrumbItem](templates/BreadcrumbItemShowcase.md) (`BreadcrumbItemShowcase`): BreadcrumbItem represents a single step in a breadcrumb trail, supporting links, icons, current-page markers, and custom link components.
- [BreadcrumbItem — Basic](templates/BreadcrumbItemBasic.md) (`BreadcrumbItemBasic`): Breadcrumb links inside a Breadcrumbs trail. Ancestor pages get an href; mark the last item with isCurrent to render it as plain text for the current page.
- [Breadcrumbs](templates/BreadcrumbsShowcase.md) (`BreadcrumbsShowcase`): A breadcrumb trail showing page hierarchy with linked ancestors and a current page.
- [Breadcrumbs — Deep Path](templates/BreadcrumbsDeepHierarchy.md) (`BreadcrumbsDeepHierarchy`): A 5-level breadcrumb trail for deeply nested content. Use in e-commerce, file browsers, or any UI with several levels of hierarchy.
- [Breadcrumbs — Icons](templates/BreadcrumbsWithIcons.md) (`BreadcrumbsWithIcons`): Add icons before breadcrumb labels for quick recognition. Use a home icon on the root item and contextual icons on key sections.
- [Breadcrumbs — Menu item](templates/BreadcrumbsMenuItem.md) (`BreadcrumbsMenuItem`): Give a mid-trail crumb a `menu` prop to turn it into a menu trigger for switching between sibling destinations. It reuses the same item API as DropdownMenu, so an existing option array (or composed item children) drops in verbatim.
- [Breadcrumbs — Separators](templates/BreadcrumbsCustomSeparator.md) (`BreadcrumbsCustomSeparator`): Swap the default "/" for a different character like chevrons, arrows, or dots. Use when the visual style of the page calls for a different separator.
- [Breadcrumbs — Variants](templates/BreadcrumbsSupportingVariant.md) (`BreadcrumbsSupportingVariant`): Compare the default and supporting variants side by side. Use the supporting variant in dense UIs like admin panels where the breadcrumb should be subtle.
- [Button — End Slot](templates/ButtonWithEndSlot.md) (`ButtonWithEndSlot`): Buttons with a trailing badge showing a count or status. Use for notification counts, unread messages, or any button that needs a visual indicator.
- [Button — Floating](templates/ButtonFloating.md) (`ButtonFloating`): A floating action button raised with `elevation="med"`. Use elevation for buttons that hover above content, like a FAB.
- [Button — Icon](templates/ButtonWithIcon.md) (`ButtonWithIcon`): Buttons with a leading icon that reinforces the label. Use when the icon helps the user identify the action faster, like a plus for "New" or a trash can for "Delete".
- [Button — Sizes](templates/ButtonSizeVariants.md) (`ButtonSizeVariants`): Small, medium, and large buttons side by side. Use small in dense UIs like toolbars, medium for most cases, and large for prominent CTAs.
- [Button — Variants](templates/ButtonShowcase.md) (`ButtonShowcase`): All four button variants side by side: primary, secondary, ghost, and destructive. A quick visual reference for choosing the right variant.
- [Button — Variants](templates/ButtonVariants.md) (`ButtonVariants`): All 4 button variants in default, disabled, and loading states. Use primary for the main action, secondary for most others, ghost for low-emphasis, and destructive for dangerous actions.
- [ButtonGroup](templates/ButtonGroupShowcase.md) (`ButtonGroupShowcase`): 
- [ButtonGroup — Basic](templates/ButtonGroupBasic.md) (`ButtonGroupBasic`): Three related actions joined into a single connected control. Provide a group label for accessibility and keep all buttons the same variant so they read as one unit.
- [ButtonGroup — Floating](templates/ButtonGroupFloating.md) (`ButtonGroupFloating`): A grouped action bar raised with `elevation="med"`. The connected buttons share one surface, so the shadow lifts them as a unit.
- [Calendar](templates/CalendarShowcase.md) (`CalendarShowcase`): An interactive single-date calendar with a selected date. Click any day to change the selection.
- [Calendar — Constraints](templates/CalendarConstraints.md) (`CalendarConstraints`): Limit which dates can be selected using min/max bounds and custom rules like weekdays only. Use for scheduling UIs where certain dates are unavailable.
- [Calendar — Range](templates/CalendarRangeWithValue.md) (`CalendarRangeWithValue`): Pick a start and end date with the range highlighted between them. Use for booking dates, time-off requests, or report filters.
- [Calendar — Single](templates/CalendarSingle.md) (`CalendarSingle`): Pick one date from a month grid. Use for appointment dates, due dates, or any field that needs a single date.
- [Calendar — Two Months](templates/CalendarTwoMonths.md) (`CalendarTwoMonths`): Two months side by side for selecting ranges that span a month boundary. Use in booking or travel UIs where check-in and check-out often fall in different months.
- [Canvas Editor](templates/canvas-editor.md) (`canvas-editor`): Layered artboard workspace: document tabs over a layer rail, a fixed-size frame you zoom on a muted backdrop, and an inspector of position, type, and filter fields that retargets to the selected layer. Objects hold a coordinate rather than reflowing, so moving one never moves another.
- [Card](templates/CardShowcase.md) (`CardShowcase`): A card with a heading and body text showing the default container style.
- [Card — Callout](templates/CardCallout.md) (`CardCallout`): Muted-variant cards for tips, notes, or supplementary information. Use when content should be visually distinct but not prominent. The muted variant uses a wash background instead of the elevated default, making it feel recessed rather than raised. Works well in sidebars, help panels, or inline callouts.
- [Card — Elevations](templates/CardElevations.md) (`CardElevations`): The four elevation levels side by side. Cards are flat by default; raise a card with `elevation` only when it needs to float above surrounding content.
- [Card — Layout](templates/CardWithInnerLayout.md) (`CardWithInnerLayout`): A card with a structured header, content area, and footer with action buttons. Use for forms, dialogs, or settings panels that need clear sections. Pair Card with Layout to get automatic dividers between header, content, and footer. The footer aligns actions to the right by default.
- [Card — Simple](templates/CardWithSimpleContent.md) (`CardWithSimpleContent`): A card with a heading and body text. Use for summaries, descriptions, or any grouped content that needs visual separation from the page. The card handles its own border, background, and padding; just pass your content as children. Set a width to constrain it, or leave it to fill the parent.
- [Card — Variants](templates/CardVariants.md) (`CardVariants`): Default, muted, and color variants side by side. Use color variants to categorize cards visually, like team colors, project tags, or content types. Each color uses the corresponding background token from the theme, so they adapt to light and dark mode automatically.
- [Card Grid](templates/library.md) (`library`): Searchable, browsable card grid with filter tabs and a real empty state: uniform tiles organized by topic, narrowing in place, with no detail surface behind them.
- [Carousel](templates/CarouselShowcase.md) (`CarouselShowcase`): A horizontal carousel of cards with scroll-snap and navigation buttons. Scroll or click the arrows to browse.
- [Carousel — Cards](templates/CarouselCards.md) (`CarouselCards`): A horizontally scrollable row of cards with snap scrolling enabled. Use for feature grids, product lists, or any set of cards that overflows the available width. The carousel adds fade edges and navigation buttons automatically.
- [Carousel — Snap](templates/CarouselSnap.md) (`CarouselSnap`): Scroll-snap carousel with navigation buttons and team member cards. Each card snaps to the start edge on scroll. Use when items should be viewed one at a time rather than as a continuous strip.
- [Center](templates/CenterShowcase.md) (`CenterShowcase`): Content centered horizontally and vertically inside a fixed-height container.
- [Center — Horizontal Center](templates/CenterHorizontal.md) (`CenterHorizontal`): A formatting control group centered with axis="horizontal" in the default horizontal writing mode. In other writing modes, Center currently follows the flex main axis rather than guaranteeing physical horizontal centering.
- [Center — Vertical & Horizontal Center](templates/CenterInsideACard.md) (`CenterInsideACard`): An empty state with an icon, heading, and description centered both vertically and horizontally inside a card. This is the most common use of Center: placing content in the middle of a fixed-height area like a panel, card, or content region. The height prop defines the centering space.
- [Centered Hero](templates/centered-hero.md) (`centered-hero`): Symmetrical centered stack (headline, short blurb, paired call-to-action buttons) resting on one wide full-bleed picture, with nothing on either flank competing.
- [ChatComposer](templates/ChatComposerShowcase.md) (`ChatComposerShowcase`): 
- [ChatComposer — Attachments](templates/ChatComposerAttachments.md) (`ChatComposerAttachments`): Chat composer with removable file tokens in a collapsible drawer. Use when users can attach files or context to their message.
- [ChatComposer — Flat](templates/ChatComposerFlat.md) (`ChatComposerFlat`): The composer is raised by default (`elevation="low"`). Set `elevation="none"` to flatten it; it then draws a border with the same rest / hover / focus treatment as a text input.
- [ChatComposer — Footer Actions](templates/ChatComposerFooterActions.md) (`ChatComposerFooterActions`): Chat composer with dropdown menus for a model selector and settings in the footer, and a mic button in the send actions slot.
- [ChatComposer — Full Featured](templates/ChatComposerFullFeatured.md) (`ChatComposerFullFeatured`): Chat composer with all slots populated: collapsible attachment drawer, header actions, context progress bar, footer dropdown menus, and mic button. Shows the maximum composer configuration.
- [ChatComposer — Simple](templates/ChatComposerSimple.md) (`ChatComposerSimple`): Minimal chat composer with a placeholder and submit handler. The simplest way to drop a message input into a page.
- [ChatComposer — Streaming](templates/ChatComposerStreaming.md) (`ChatComposerStreaming`): Chat composer with streaming state and a stop button. Use when the assistant is generating a response and the user can cancel.
- [ChatComposer — Validation](templates/ChatComposerValidation.md) (`ChatComposerValidation`): Chat composer with error and warning status messages. Status can appear above or below the composer to surface validation or system feedback.
- [ChatComposerDrawer](templates/ChatComposerDrawerShowcase.md) (`ChatComposerDrawerShowcase`): Composer drawer with file tokens, a collapsible toggle, and header actions. Use as a starting point for any chat composer with attachments.
- [ChatComposerDrawer — Attachments](templates/ChatComposerDrawerAttachments.md) (`ChatComposerDrawerAttachments`): Drawer with two rows: a scrollable carousel of image thumbnails and a row of removable file tokens. Omit count to keep the drawer always expanded.
- [ChatComposerDrawer — Collapsible](templates/ChatComposerDrawerCollapsible.md) (`ChatComposerDrawerCollapsible`): Drawer with many items and a collapse toggle. Pass count to enable the toggle; collapsed state shows a badge with the total count and a label.
- [ChatComposerDrawer — Feedback](templates/ChatComposerDrawerFeedback.md) (`ChatComposerDrawerFeedback`): Chat composer drawer with a feedback prompt and selectable lettered options. Use for user confirmation workflows that require explicit action before proceeding.
- [ChatComposerDrawer — With Progress](templates/ChatComposerDrawerWithProgress.md) (`ChatComposerDrawerWithProgress`): Drawer paired with a context progress bar in the header. Show context window usage when attachments consume part of the available token budget.
- [ChatComposerInput](templates/ChatComposerInputShowcase.md) (`ChatComposerInputShowcase`): 
- [ChatComposerInput — Controlled](templates/ChatComposerInputControlledInput.md) (`ChatComposerInputControlledInput`): Controlled chat input with live value display. Use controlled mode when you need to read or transform the input value outside the composer.
- [ChatComposerInput — Disabled](templates/ChatComposerInputDisabled.md) (`ChatComposerInputDisabled`): Composer in a disabled state. Use when the input should be visible but not interactive, such as during streaming or when a prerequisite is unmet.
- [ChatComposerInput — Mentions](templates/ChatComposerInputMentionTrigger.md) (`ChatComposerInputMentionTrigger`): Chat input with an @ trigger that opens a typeahead menu for mentioning users. Selected names appear as inline tokens.
- [ChatComposerInput — Multiple Triggers](templates/ChatComposerInputMultipleTriggers.md) (`ChatComposerInputMultipleTriggers`): Chat input with both @ mentions and / commands. Each trigger type renders tokens in a distinct color so users can tell them apart at a glance.
- [ChatComposerInput — Slash Commands](templates/ChatComposerInputSlashCommands.md) (`ChatComposerInputSlashCommands`): Chat input with a / trigger for command selection. Use for AI assistants or bots that support structured commands.
- [ChatDictationButton](templates/ChatDictationButtonShowcase.md) (`ChatDictationButtonShowcase`): Interactive dictation button connected to the SpeechRecognition API via useChatDictation. Click the mic to dictate into the composer.
- [ChatDictationButton — Basic](templates/ChatDictationButtonBasic.md) (`ChatDictationButtonBasic`): A dictation button wired to useChatDictation and placed in the sendActions slot of a ChatComposer. Click the microphone to transcribe speech into the input.
- [ChatDictationButton — In Composer](templates/ChatDictationDictationInComposer.md) (`ChatDictationDictationInComposer`): Dictation button placed in the sendActions slot of a chat composer. Shows the recommended integration point for voice input alongside the send button.
- [ChatDictationButton — Sizes](templates/ChatDictationSizes.md) (`ChatDictationSizes`): Small and medium dictation buttons side by side. Use small in compact composer densities and medium for standard layouts.
