- [SegmentedControl — With Icons](templates/SegmentedControlWithIcons.md) (`SegmentedControlWithIcons`): Segmented control with icon and label pairs for a view mode switcher.
- [SegmentedControlItem](templates/SegmentedControlItemShowcase.md) (`SegmentedControlItemShowcase`): Segmented control items with text labels and icons, including a disabled item.
- [SegmentedControlItem — Basic](templates/SegmentedControlItemBasic.md) (`SegmentedControlItemBasic`): A row of label-only options that switches between a few views, here Board, List, and Timeline. Each item declares a value; the parent control holds the selected value and change handler.
- [SelectableCard](templates/SelectableCardShowcase.md) (`SelectableCardShowcase`): A plan picker with single-select radio behavior. Cards show an accent border when selected.
- [SelectableCard — Elevated](templates/SelectableCardElevated.md) (`SelectableCardElevated`): Raised selectable cards with `elevation="low"`. The inset selection ring composes on top of the shadow, so a selected card keeps its elevation.
- [SelectableCardMulti](templates/SelectableCardMulti.md) (`SelectableCardMulti`): Multi-select tag picker using color variant selectable cards with color-matched selection borders.
- [Selector](templates/SelectorShowcase.md) (`SelectorShowcase`): 
- [Selector — Bottom Sheet](templates/SelectorBottomSheet.md) (`SelectorBottomSheet`): Presents a single-selection list in a bottom sheet for compact touch interfaces.
- [Selector — Clearable](templates/SelectorClearable.md) (`SelectorClearable`): Selector with a clear button to reset the selected value.
- [Selector — Ghost Toolbar](templates/SelectorGhostToolbar.md) (`SelectorGhostToolbar`): Borderless Selector variant composed with ghost buttons in a toolbar.
- [Selector — Grouped Sections](templates/SelectorWithSections.md) (`SelectorWithSections`): Selector with options grouped into labeled sections.
- [Selector — Option descriptions](templates/SelectorOptionDescriptions.md) (`SelectorOptionDescriptions`): Options carry a description, so the dropdown draws a two-line row. The closed trigger is sized by padding, so it is the size token for a one-line value and exactly one line taller for a two-line one; both on the 4px rhythm. An InputGroup pins the row, so the value folds back onto one line there.
- [Selector — Validation States](templates/SelectorWithStatus.md) (`SelectorWithStatus`): Selector showing error, warning, and success validation states.
- [SelectorOption](templates/SelectorOptionShowcase.md) (`SelectorOptionShowcase`): Selector with custom-rendered options using SelectorOption for icons and descriptions.
- [SelectorOption — Basic](templates/SelectorOptionBasic.md) (`SelectorOptionBasic`): A selector whose options are rendered with SelectorOption, adding a secondary description below each label. Use inside renderOption for consistent custom option styling.
- [Service Monitoring Dashboard](templates/dashboard-alert-rail.md) (`dashboard-alert-rail`): Always-on analytics with a triage rail: status-colored tiles with sparklines, multi-series time charts over a switchable window, and an independently scrolling alert column that folds into the content when narrow.
- [Settings Dialog](templates/settings-dialog.md) (`settings-dialog`): Preferences inside a modal container with searchable section navigation, so configuration happens without leaving whatever is underneath. Grouped toggles, live preview of appearance choices, rebindable shortcuts.
- [Settings Form](templates/settings.md) (`settings`): Preferences as one continuously scrolling form, sections stacked in order with no navigation between them. The simplest settings shape: everything reachable by scrolling.
- [Settings Panels](templates/settings-sidebar.md) (`settings-sidebar`): Preferences split into nav-switched panels: a persistent section list swaps the pane beside it, and rows edit in place rather than opening a separate form.
- [Shell Nav](templates/shell-nav.md) (`shell-nav`): Application frame combining both navigation axes: a top menu bar with command-palette search over a resizable hierarchy rail, wrapping placeholder content. For when one axis is not enough.
- [Side Gallery](templates/side-gallery.md) (`side-gallery`): Asymmetric split section: a copy column of headline, supporting text, and links held against a clustered image collage opposite. Deliberately off-balance, unlike the centered hero.
- [Side Nav](templates/shell-side-nav.md) (`shell-side-nav`): Application frame with a single collapsible, resizable left rail carrying grouped history and search, wrapping the main content. Vertical navigation only, no top bar.
- [SideNav](templates/SideNavShowcase.md) (`SideNavShowcase`): 
- [SideNav — End Content](templates/SideNavEndContent.md) (`SideNavEndContent`): Side navigation items with badges, counts, and context menus as trailing content.
- [SideNav — Header with Menu](templates/SideNavWithHeaderMenu.md) (`SideNavWithHeaderMenu`): Side navigation with an account switcher dropdown in the header for multi-account apps.
- [SideNav — Nested Items](templates/SideNavNestedItems.md) (`SideNavNestedItems`): Side navigation with collapsible nested items for settings or hierarchical menus.
- [SideNavCollapseButton](templates/SideNavCollapseButtonShowcase.md) (`SideNavCollapseButtonShowcase`): Demonstrates SideNavCollapseButton inside a collapsible SideNav.
- [SideNavCollapseButton — Basic](templates/SideNavCollapseButtonBasic.md) (`SideNavCollapseButtonBasic`): Place a collapse button in the SideNav footer to let users toggle the rail between expanded and collapsed states. Disable the built-in button via collapsible={{hasButton: false}} when positioning it yourself.
- [SideNavHeading](templates/SideNavHeadingShowcase.md) (`SideNavHeadingShowcase`): Demonstrates SideNavHeading with an app name, logo icon, superheading, and subheading.
- [SideNavHeading — Basic](templates/SideNavHeadingBasic.md) (`SideNavHeadingBasic`): A SideNav header with an app icon and a linked title. Pass it to the SideNav header prop to identify the product or workspace at the top of the navigation rail.
- [SideNavItem](templates/SideNavItemShowcase.md) (`SideNavItemShowcase`): Demonstrates SideNavItem with selected, icon, disabled, and nested states.
- [SideNavItem — Basic](templates/SideNavItemBasic.md) (`SideNavItemBasic`): Navigation links inside a SideNav, each with a label, an icon, and an href. Mark the item for the current page with isSelected.
- [SideNavSection](templates/SideNavSectionShowcase.md) (`SideNavSectionShowcase`): Demonstrates SideNavSection with titled groups of navigation items.
- [SideNavSection — Basic](templates/SideNavSectionBasic.md) (`SideNavSectionBasic`): Group related SideNavItems under titled sections. Use sections to organize longer navigation lists into scannable clusters like Overview and Account.
- [Simple Table](templates/table.md) (`table`): Flat row collection where columns sort, rows select into a bulk-action toolbar, and each row carries an overflow menu. Sortable but ungrouped, with no detail pane, the baseline shape.
- [Skeleton](templates/SkeletonShowcase.md) (`SkeletonShowcase`): A skeleton loading placeholder.
- [Skeleton — Card Loading](templates/SkeletonCardSkeleton.md) (`SkeletonCardSkeleton`): Card skeleton with avatar, name, and content lines.
- [Skeleton — Staggered List](templates/SkeletonStaggeredList.md) (`SkeletonStaggeredList`): Staggered skeleton lines with varying widths.
- [Skeleton — Table Rows](templates/SkeletonTableRowSkeleton.md) (`SkeletonTableRowSkeleton`): Table skeleton with staggered column widths.
- [Slide in from the start edge](templates/DrawerStart.md) (`DrawerStart`): Set side="start" to open from the inline start edge: left in LTR and right in RTL. The default end edge follows the inspector convention.
- [Slider](templates/SliderShowcase.md) (`SliderShowcase`): A slider control set to 50%.
- [Slider — Formatted Value](templates/SliderFormattedValue.md) (`SliderFormattedValue`): Slider with custom formatting showing temperature in Fahrenheit.
- [Slider — Range](templates/SliderRangeSlider.md) (`SliderRangeSlider`): Range slider for selecting a value range like price bounds.
- [Slider — Validation States](templates/SliderWithStatus.md) (`SliderWithStatus`): Sliders with error, warning, and success validation states.
- [Slider — With Marks](templates/SliderWithMarks.md) (`SliderWithMarks`): Slider with labeled tick marks at fixed intervals.
- [Spinner](templates/SpinnerShowcase.md) (`SpinnerShowcase`): A large spinner indicator.
- [Spinner — On Media Shade](templates/SpinnerOnMedia.md) (`SpinnerOnMedia`): Default and onMedia shade spinners for light and dark backgrounds.
- [Spinner — Sizes](templates/SpinnerSizes.md) (`SpinnerSizes`): All spinner sizes displayed side by side.
- [Spinner — With Label](templates/SpinnerWithLabel.md) (`SpinnerWithLabel`): Spinners with text and rich multi-line labels.
- [Stack — Alignment](templates/StackAlignment.md) (`StackAlignment`): Buttons positioned at the start, center, and end of a row.
- [Stack — Directions](templates/StackDirections.md) (`StackDirections`): Badges arranged horizontally and vertically in side-by-side cards.
- [Stack — Fill Item](templates/StackFillItem.md) (`StackFillItem`): An avatar, text, and button in a row; the text stretches to fill the available space.
- [StackItem](templates/StackItemShowcase.md) (`StackItemShowcase`): StackItem can be used within HStack or VStack for more granular control over individual item sizing and alignment, but is optional; stack children work without it.
- [StackItem — Fill](templates/StackItemFill.md) (`StackItemFill`): A static-width item next to one that fills the remaining space. Wrap stack children in StackItem when an item needs explicit sizing control.
- [StatusDot](templates/StatusDotShowcase.md) (`StatusDotShowcase`): A positive status dot indicator.
- [StatusDot — Pulsing](templates/StatusDotPulsing.md) (`StatusDotPulsing`): Animated pulsing dots for live, processing, and error states.
- [StatusDot — Status Indicators](templates/StatusDotStatusIndicators.md) (`StatusDotStatusIndicators`): Labeled status dot list for presence indicators like online, away, and offline.
- [StatusDot — Variants](templates/StatusDotVariants.md) (`StatusDotVariants`): All five semantic color variants displayed in a row.
- [Step](templates/StepShowcase.md) (`StepShowcase`): A single Step, with every part it can render: the indicator, the label with its optional marker and trailing endContent, and the description beneath. A Step never sets its own completed/current state. It declares its index and derives the rest from the parent Stepper, so one Step in one Stepper is a complete example.
- [Step — Content Slot](templates/StepContent.md) (`StepContent`): Children passed to a Step render below its description, indented to line up with the label rather than the indicator, and stay outside the clickable label area so buttons inside remain their own targets. In a full flow you gate the slot on the step being active. That is what turns a vertical stepper into an expanding one.
- [Step — Indicator](templates/StepIndicator.md) (`StepIndicator`): Everything the indicator prop accepts: the auto default, an always-number badge, a custom ReactNode, and none, each on its own completed Step so the prop is the only difference between them. Every variant occupies the same 16px box, so a step swapping its number for a check as it completes never shifts the label beside it. The last cell shows that a custom node can be live rather than static: a Spinner on a step that is in progress, shaded `inherit` so it picks up the step's own tint like any other glyph.
- [Step — States](templates/StepStates.md) (`StepStates`): Every state a single Step can land in, each shown as one Step in its own Stepper. Completed, current, and upcoming are derived by comparing the step index against the parent activeStep, so they are never set directly; isDisabled and status are the two a step declares itself. Status is a separate axis from progress, which is why a completed step can still carry a warning.
- [Stepper — Checkout Progress](templates/StepperShowcase.md) (`StepperShowcase`): The default stepper: a horizontal track where every step owns an equal segment of the progress bar above its label. The default auto indicator resolves itself per step: a check once the step is done, a ring on the current step, a number for the ones still ahead. Click any step to jump.
- [Stepper — Custom Content](templates/StepperCustomContent.md) (`StepperCustomContent`): A vertical stepper where each step owns a slice of the page. The content slot takes any node (form fields, a summary panel, a banner), so a stepper is not limited to multi-step forms. Rendering the slot only for the active step is what makes the flow expand one step at a time.
- [Stepper — Horizontal Narrow Collapsed](templates/StepperWidthResponsiveCollapse.md) (`StepperWidthResponsiveCollapse`): A narrow horizontal stepper using horizontalOptions. At 320px wide, four steps fall below the 112px minimumStepWidth and collapse into a current-step summary with Previous and Next controls.
- [Stepper — Indicator Modes](templates/StepperIndicatorModes.md) (`StepperIndicatorModes`): The indicator prop side by side: none (the bar and label carry the progress on their own), auto (check when done, ring when current, number ahead), always-number, and a custom icon per step.
- [Stepper — On-Track Horizontal](templates/StepperOnTrackHorizontal.md) (`StepperOnTrackHorizontal`): The on-track layout in horizontal orientation: instead of sitting beside the label, each indicator is slotted into the connector itself, so the numbered nodes read as beads on one continuous line. Labels center under their node.
- [Stepper — On-Track Vertical](templates/StepperOnTrackVertical.md) (`StepperOnTrackVertical`): The on-track layout in vertical orientation: indicators sit inline on a continuous connector rail, with each label and description beside its node. Compare with the separated layout, where the indicator sits alongside its own bar segment instead of on a shared rail.
- [Stepper — Validation Status](templates/StepperStatus.md) (`StepperStatus`): Semantic status per step in a verification flow: success shows a green check, error a red glyph, accent the in-progress step. Status sets the indicator color and glyph only, never the connector, and is announced to assistive tech as text.
- [Switch](templates/SwitchShowcase.md) (`SwitchShowcase`): A toggle switch for enabling notifications.
- [Switch — Disabled](templates/SwitchDisabled.md) (`SwitchDisabled`): Disabled switch with label and description for gated features.
- [Switch — Settings Panel](templates/SwitchSettingsPanel.md) (`SwitchSettingsPanel`): Settings panel with spread-spaced switches in a card.
- [Switch — With Description](templates/SwitchWithDescription.md) (`SwitchWithDescription`): Toggle with a label and supporting description text.
- [Switch — With Status](templates/SwitchWithStatus.md) (`SwitchWithStatus`): Switches with error, warning, and success validation states.
- [SyntaxTheme — Compact Preset](templates/SyntaxThemeShowcase.md) (`SyntaxThemeShowcase`): A concise code block rendered with the One Dark Pro syntax preset to show how SyntaxTheme changes highlighting colors without making the page long.
- [SyntaxTheme — Dark Preset](templates/SyntaxThemeDarkPreset.md) (`SyntaxThemeDarkPreset`): Wrap a code block in SyntaxTheme to apply a dark syntax preset such as Dracula.
- [SyntaxTheme — Light Preset](templates/SyntaxThemeLightPreset.md) (`SyntaxThemeLightPreset`): Use a light syntax preset for code examples that need to sit on light documentation surfaces.
- [Tab](templates/TabShowcase.md) (`TabShowcase`): Tab is an individual tab item within a TabList, supporting labels, icons, selected icons, and end content slots.
- [Tab — Selected Icon](templates/TabWithSelectedIcon.md) (`TabWithSelectedIcon`): A tab that changes its icon when selected.
- [Table](templates/TableShowcase.md) (`TableShowcase`): Data-driven table with proportional and pixel column widths and hover highlighting.
- [Table — Column Settings](templates/TableColumnSettingsTable.md) (`TableColumnSettingsTable`): Table with a column visibility picker in the toolbar. Toggle columns on and off.
- [Table — Grid Dividers](templates/TableGridDividersTable.md) (`TableGridDividersTable`): Compact table with grid dividers showing both row and column borders, suited for dense numeric data.
- [Table — In Card](templates/TableInCard.md) (`TableInCard`): Table composed inside a card with a heading, demonstrating container bleed alignment.
- [Table — Inline Filters](templates/TableInlineFilterTable.md) (`TableInlineFilterTable`): Table with inline filter controls rendered directly below each column header.
- [Table — Paginated Data](templates/TablePaginatedTable.md) (`TablePaginatedTable`): Paginated data table navigating through a larger dataset page by page.
- [Table — Popover Filters](templates/TableFilterableTable.md) (`TableFilterableTable`): Table with popover filter controls triggered by icons in column headers.
- [Table — Resizable Columns](templates/TableResizableTable.md) (`TableResizableTable`): Table with draggable column resize handles. Drag the right edge of any header to resize.
- [Table — Rich Cell Content](templates/TableRichCellTable.md) (`TableRichCellTable`): Table with rich cell content using Link for emails and Badge for role labels.
- [Table — Row Selection](templates/TableSelectableTable.md) (`TableSelectableTable`): Table with row selection checkboxes and a select-all header checkbox.
- [Table — Selection in the Leading Mark](templates/TableLeadingMarkSelection.md) (`TableLeadingMarkSelection`): Selection without a checkbox column: each item shows its avatar, and the checkbox takes the avatar slot while a mouse is over it, on keyboard focus, and everywhere once anything is selected; on touch screens it always shows. The state comes from useTableSelectionState, and the checkboxes render in the name column instead of the useTableSelection column, so checked items get no aria-selected or highlight; add them if needed.
- [Table — Sortable Columns](templates/TableSortableTable.md) (`TableSortableTable`): Table with sortable columns, click headers to sort ascending or descending.
- [Table — Striped Rows](templates/TableStripedTable.md) (`TableStripedTable`): Table with alternating row colors and hover highlighting for easy scanning.
- [Table: Bulk Actions](templates/TableBulkActionsTable.md) (`TableBulkActionsTable`): Controlled row selection with the reusable TableSelectionToolbar rendered in flow above the table. Product actions occupy the logical start; synchronized selection count and complete clear action occupy the logical end.
- [Table: Floating Bulk Actions](templates/TableFloatingBulkActionsTable.md) (`TableFloatingBulkActionsTable`): The reusable TableSelectionToolbar inside a capped, self-contained scroll region for a long non-sticky table below metric cards. The caller-owned sticky placement keeps actions 16px from the example scrollport without moving the table when selection changes.
- [TabList](templates/TabListShowcase.md) (`TabListShowcase`): 
- [TabList — Fill Layout](templates/TabListTabsFillLayout.md) (`TabListTabsFillLayout`): Tabs that stretch to fill the available width with a bottom divider.
- [TabList — With Actions](templates/TabListTabsWithActions.md) (`TabListTabsWithActions`): Page header pattern with tabs on the left and action buttons pushed to the right. When hasDivider is true, match the Button size to the TabList size so the tabs and actions align to a shared baseline above the divider.
- [TabList — With Badge](templates/TabListTabsWithBadge.md) (`TabListTabsWithBadge`): Tabs with notification badge counts rendered via endContent. Uses error variant for urgent counts and neutral for informational ones.
- [TabList — With Icons](templates/TabListTabsWithIcons.md) (`TabListTabsWithIcons`): Tabs with leading icons alongside text labels.
- [TabList — With Overflow Menu](templates/TabListTabsWithMenu.md) (`TabListTabsWithMenu`): Tab list with a dropdown menu for additional items that do not fit inline.
- [TabList — With Status Dot](templates/TabListTabsWithStatusDot.md) (`TabListTabsWithStatusDot`): Tabs with status dot indicators rendered via endContent to show live environment health at a glance.
- [TabMenu](templates/TabMenuShowcase.md) (`TabMenuShowcase`): TabMenu is an overflow menu within a TabList that groups additional tab options into a dropdown, showing the selected option's label as the trigger text.
- [TabMenu — Basic](templates/TabMenuBasic.md) (`TabMenuBasic`): An overflow menu at the end of a TabList that collects secondary tabs behind a dropdown. Use it when there are more tabs than fit comfortably inline.
- [Text](templates/TextShowcase.md) (`TextShowcase`): 
- [Text — Colors](templates/TextColors.md) (`TextColors`): All text color options (primary, secondary, disabled, placeholder, active) applied to body text to show their intended use.
- [Text — Heading Levels](templates/TextHeadingLevels.md) (`TextHeadingLevels`): All 6 heading levels (h1 through h6) rendered with Heading to show the full type scale.
- [Text — Inline](templates/TextInline.md) (`TextInline`): Mixing body and code text inline within a single line using the default inline display mode.
- [Text — Truncation](templates/TextTruncation.md) (`TextTruncation`): Single-line and multi-line text truncation with ellipsis using maxLines in a width-constrained container.
- [Text — Types](templates/TextTypes.md) (`TextTypes`): All 5 semantic text types (body, large, label, supporting, code) with their default styling from the theme.
- [Text — Weight](templates/TextWeight.md) (`TextWeight`): The 4 font weight variants (normal, medium, semibold, bold) applied to body text.
- [Text — Word Break](templates/TextWordBreak.md) (`TextWordBreak`): Compares break-word and break-all word break modes on a long unbreakable string.
- [Text — Wrap](templates/TextWrap.md) (`TextWrap`): The 4 text-wrap modes (wrap, nowrap, balance, pretty) shown in width-constrained containers.
- [TextArea](templates/TextAreaShowcase.md) (`TextAreaShowcase`): A text area with placeholder text.
- [TextArea — Character Count](templates/TextAreaCharacterCount.md) (`TextAreaCharacterCount`): Textareas with maxLength and a live character counter. The counter turns red when the limit is exceeded.
- [TextArea — Icon](templates/TextAreaWithIcon.md) (`TextAreaWithIcon`): Textareas with a leading icon that hints at the expected content, like a chat bubble for messages or a pencil for notes.
- [TextArea — States](templates/TextAreaStates.md) (`TextAreaStates`): Required, disabled, and loading textareas side by side. Shows the interactive states the component supports.
- [TextArea — Validation](templates/TextAreaValidation.md) (`TextAreaValidation`): All three status variants (error, warning, and success) with status messages, plus error without a message. Use to show inline validation feedback as the user types.
- [TextInput](templates/TextInputShowcase.md) (`TextInputShowcase`): 
- [TextInput — Icon](templates/TextInputIcon.md) (`TextInputIcon`): Inputs with a leading icon that hints at the expected content. Use when the icon helps users identify the field faster, like a lock for passwords or an envelope for email.
- [TextInput — Search](templates/TextInputSearch.md) (`TextInputSearch`): Search input with a hidden label, start icon, and clear button. Use for toolbar and header search bars where the icon provides sufficient context.
- [TextInput — Sizes](templates/TextInputSizes.md) (`TextInputSizes`): Small, medium, and large inputs side by side. Use small in dense UIs like table filters, medium for most forms, and large for prominent single-field pages.
- [TextInput — States](templates/TextInputStates.md) (`TextInputStates`): Error, warning, and success validation states with status messages. Use to show users what went wrong and how to fix it.
- [TextInput — Status variant](templates/TextInputStatusVariant.md) (`TextInputStatusVariant`): The statusVariant prop controls whether the status message is attached to the bordered input (default, overlapping directly below) or detached from it (floating below as a separate element with spacing).
- [TextInput — Types](templates/TextInputTypes.md) (`TextInputTypes`): Text, password, and email types plus field-level features: tooltip, required, optional, description, disabled, and loading.
- [Theme — Apply Theme](templates/ThemeApply.md) (`ThemeApply`): Wrap a subtree in Theme to apply a theme to every child component in that region.
- [Theme — Distinct Themes](templates/ThemeShowcase.md) (`ThemeShowcase`): Two visually distinct theme providers wrapping identical content to show how Theme changes the visual treatment of child components.
- [Theme — Nested Theme](templates/ThemeNested.md) (`ThemeNested`): Nested Theme providers let a local region use a different theme without affecting the rest of the page.
- [Theme — Switch Themes](templates/ThemeSwitcher.md) (`ThemeSwitcher`): Use state to switch the theme object passed to Theme and preview a different visual treatment.
- [Theme Showcase](templates/theme-showcase.md) (`theme-showcase`): Multi-surface comparison shell: preview palettes, typography, icons and control states across a storefront, checkout, chat and inventory on one responsive canvas. A theme preview and design-system showcase, with an embeddable content view for an existing app shell.
- [Thumbnail](templates/ThumbnailShowcase.md) (`ThumbnailShowcase`): A thumbnail with an image and label.
- [Thumbnail — Disabled](templates/ThumbnailDisabled.md) (`ThumbnailDisabled`): Thumbnails in the disabled state with reduced opacity. The open and remove buttons stay focusable and announced as disabled, and call nothing.
- [Thumbnail — Gallery](templates/ThumbnailGallery.md) (`ThumbnailGallery`): A row of clickable thumbnails with labels that open a detail view. Use for image attachment lists where users need to preview and manage uploads.
- [Thumbnail — Removable](templates/ThumbnailRemovable.md) (`ThumbnailRemovable`): Thumbnails with a remove button overlay. The close button uses APCA luminance detection to stay visible on both dark and light images.
- [Thumbnail — States](templates/ThumbnailStates.md) (`ThumbnailStates`): All visual states side by side: image loaded, placeholder, skeleton loading, and upload overlay. Demonstrates the full lifecycle of a thumbnail from empty to loaded.
- [TimeInput](templates/TimeInputShowcase.md) (`TimeInputShowcase`): A time input that uses the browser/OS picker on touch by default and Astryx typed entry on fine pointers.
- [TimeInput — Constrained](templates/TimeInputConstrained.md) (`TimeInputConstrained`): Time inputs with min/max constraints limiting selection to specific windows. Use to prevent out-of-bounds selections for appointments, reservations, or shift scheduling.
- [TimeInput — Formats](templates/TimeInputFormats.md) (`TimeInputFormats`): 12-hour, 24-hour, and seconds formats side by side. Use 12h for US-centric UIs, 24h for international or technical contexts, and seconds for precise timing.
- [TimeInput — Increment](templates/TimeInputIncrement.md) (`TimeInputIncrement`): Time input with a custom step increment. Arrow keys jump by the specified interval (e.g. 15 minutes) for quick slot-based scheduling.
- [TimeInput — States](templates/TimeInputStates.md) (`TimeInputStates`): Default, disabled, error, warning, and success states. Use status messages to give users clear feedback about their time selection.
- [Timer](templates/TimerShowcase.md) (`TimerShowcase`): 
- [Timer — Formats](templates/TimerFormats.md) (`TimerFormats`): Elapsed compact units and stopwatch clock notation shown from the same start time.
- [Timer — Inline](templates/TimerInline.md) (`TimerInline`): A Timer composed into status copy while inheriting the surrounding typography.
- [Timer — Typography](templates/TimerTypography.md) (`TimerTypography`): Timer using its Timestamp-matched default typography and an emphasized override.
- [Timestamp](templates/TimestampShowcase.md) (`TimestampShowcase`): 
- [Timestamp — Auto](templates/TimestampAutoFormat.md) (`TimestampAutoFormat`): Auto format that shows relative time for recent dates and switches to the full date for older ones. The default choice for most use cases.
- [Timestamp — Colors](templates/TimestampColors.md) (`TimestampColors`): Timestamp rendered in each available color variant: primary, secondary, disabled, and active.
- [Timestamp — Formats](templates/TimestampFormats.md) (`TimestampFormats`): All display formats side by side: date, date_time, time, and their system equivalents. Use date and date_time for user-facing UI, system variants for logs and dev tools.
- [Timestamp — Relative](templates/TimestampRelativeFormat.md) (`TimestampRelativeFormat`): Relative time labels from seconds to months ago, with hover tooltips showing the full date. Use in feeds, comment threads, and activity logs.
- [Timestamp — Timezone](templates/TimestampTimezone.md) (`TimestampTimezone`): Timestamps with the timezone abbreviation appended. Enable isTimezoneShown for audiences across time zones, like audit logs or team calendars.
- [Timestamp — Tooltip time zones](templates/TimestampTooltipTimezones.md) (`TimestampTooltipTimezones`): Hover tooltips that show one instant across several time zones or formats. Use tooltipEntries when readers must compare zones, like an incident log carrying both the reader's time and the event's origin zone.
- [Toast](templates/ToastShowcase.md) (`ToastShowcase`): Imperative toast notifications triggered with useToast and rendered in the toast viewport.
- [Toast — Action](templates/ToastAction.md) (`ToastAction`): Persistent toasts with a trailing button or link so the user can act on the notification, like undoing a delete or viewing a report.
- [Toast — Deduplication](templates/ToastDeduplication.md) (`ToastDeduplication`): Prevent duplicate toasts with uniqueID. Use ignore to keep the first toast, or overwrite to replace it with updated content like a progress percentage.
- [Toast — Dismiss](templates/ToastDismiss.md) (`ToastDismiss`): Show a persistent toast and dismiss it programmatically using the function returned by useToast. Use for long-running operations that need manual cleanup.
- [Toast — Stacking](templates/ToastStacking.md) (`ToastStacking`): Multiple toasts stacking vertically with smooth enter and exit animations. Click repeatedly to see how toasts queue and dismiss.
- [Toast — Types](templates/ToastTypes.md) (`ToastTypes`): Info and error toast variants side by side. Info toasts auto-dismiss after 5 seconds, error toasts persist until the user dismisses them.
- [ToggleButton](templates/ToggleButtonShowcase.md) (`ToggleButtonShowcase`): 
- [ToggleButton — Color](templates/ToggleButtonColor.md) (`ToggleButtonColor`): Toggle buttons with colored icons in the pressed state. Shows accent-colored toolbar formatting and semantic reaction colors (yellow star, red heart, blue bookmark).
- [ToggleButton — Group](templates/ToggleButtonGroup.md) (`ToggleButtonGroup`): Toggle button groups in single-select and multi-select modes. Single selection acts as a view mode switcher; multiple selection forms a formatting toolbar.
- [ToggleButton — Icon Swap](templates/ToggleButtonIconSwap.md) (`ToggleButtonIconSwap`): Icon-only toggle buttons that swap between outline and solid icons when pressed. Use for actions like favorite, bookmark, or mute where the icon itself communicates the state.
- [ToggleButton — Label](templates/ToggleButtonLabel.md) (`ToggleButtonLabel`): Toggle buttons with visible text labels that show a font weight shift on press. Use when the icon alone is not enough to communicate the action.
- [ToggleButton — States](templates/ToggleButtonStates.md) (`ToggleButtonStates`): Default, pressed, disabled, and loading states of a standalone toggle button. Shows how visual treatment changes across states.
- [ToggleButtonGroup](templates/ToggleButtonGroupShowcase.md) (`ToggleButtonGroupShowcase`): ToggleButtonGroup manages a set of ToggleButtons with single-select or multi-select behavior for options like view modes or filters.
- [ToggleButtonGroup — Vertical](templates/ToggleButtonGroupVertical.md) (`ToggleButtonGroupVertical`): A vertically stacked ToggleButtonGroup using the vertical orientation, shown with both single-select and multi-select behavior, ideal for sidebar-style option lists and vertical toolbars.
- [Token](templates/TokenShowcase.md) (`TokenShowcase`): 
- [Token — Clickable](templates/TokenClickable.md) (`TokenClickable`): Interactive tokens that respond to clicks. Use for toggleable filters or tokens that open a detail view when selected.
- [Token — Colors](templates/TokenColors.md) (`TokenColors`): All 11 color variants in default and disabled states. Use color to categorize entities or convey status at a glance.
- [Token — End Content](templates/TokenEndContent.md) (`TokenEndContent`): Tokens with trailing content like a count badge or status indicator after the label. Use for notification counts, item quantities, or compact status info.
- [Token — Icon](templates/TokenIcon.md) (`TokenIcon`): Tokens with a leading icon that identifies the entity type. Use when the icon helps users recognize the token category faster, like a user icon for people or a tag icon for labels.
- [Token — Removable](templates/TokenRemovable.md) (`TokenRemovable`): Tokens with a dismiss button for selections the user can undo. Use in multi-select fields, active filters, or any list of user-chosen items.
- [Tokenizer](templates/TokenizerShowcase.md) (`TokenizerShowcase`): A tokenizer with preset tags and search source.
- [Tokenizer — Clear](templates/TokenizerClear.md) (`TokenizerClear`): Tokenizer with a built-in clear-all button for bulk removal of all selected tokens. On touch screens, clear through the sheet's Clear all.
- [Tokenizer — Creatable](templates/TokenizerCreatable.md) (`TokenizerCreatable`): Free-text tokenizer for creating custom tags and a combined create-or-search pattern. Use when users need to enter values that may not exist in a predefined list.
- [Tokenizer — End Content](templates/TokenizerEndContent.md) (`TokenizerEndContent`): Tokenizer with an action button in the end slot. Use for inline actions like applying selections alongside the input.
- [Tokenizer — Icon](templates/TokenizerIcon.md) (`TokenizerIcon`): Tokenizer with a leading search icon to visually reinforce the search behavior.
- [Tokenizer — Max Entries](templates/TokenizerMaxEntries.md) (`TokenizerMaxEntries`): Tokenizer with a maximum selection limit. The input hides automatically when the limit is reached, preventing further additions.
- [Tokenizer — Overflow](templates/TokenizerOverflow.md) (`TokenizerOverflow`): Tokenizer with overflow truncation when unfocused. Inline mode pushes content down on expand; layer mode overlays without shifting layout. Overflow modes apply to the inline field.
- [Tokenizer — States](templates/TokenizerStates.md) (`TokenizerStates`): Tokenizer in disabled, error, warning, and success states. Use to communicate validation feedback or lock a selection from editing.
- [Toolbar — Bulk Actions](templates/ToolbarBulkActions.md) (`ToolbarBulkActions`): A compact toolbar with the muted variant for showing bulk selection actions. Use when the user selects multiple items in a list or table and needs quick access to batch operations.
- [Toolbar — Card Header](templates/ToolbarCardHeader.md) (`ToolbarCardHeader`): A toolbar as a card header with a left-aligned title and icon actions on the right. Use Toolbar instead of LayoutHeader when your card header has interactive actions; Toolbar adds start/end slot layout, keyboard navigation, and automatic size cascading. If the header is just a title with no actions, a LayoutHeader or Section is enough.
- [Toolbar — Sizes](templates/ToolbarSizes.md) (`ToolbarSizes`): Small, medium, and large toolbars side by side. The size prop cascades to child buttons and inputs automatically. Use small in dense UIs like cards, medium for most cases, and large for spacious layouts.
- [Toolbar — Tab Navigation](templates/ToolbarWithTabs.md) (`ToolbarWithTabs`): A toolbar with tabs in the start slot and an action button at the end. Use as a card or section header when content is split into tabs with a primary action alongside.
- [Toolbar — Table Filter](templates/ToolbarTableFilter.md) (`ToolbarTableFilter`): Filter bar above a table: a search box leads the row, each field beside it is a closed trigger that doubles as its own filter chip — the bare field name unset, the whole clause once set — and the clauses fold from the end into a count as the row narrows, followed by a live result count, a clear all, and a column picker. Use to search, filter, and narrow flat rows of records such as jobs, orders, tickets, or users.
- [Toolbar — Three Slot](templates/ToolbarThreeSlot.md) (`ToolbarThreeSlot`): A toolbar with start, center, and end content using the three-column grid layout. Use when you need a centered title or heading with navigation and actions on either side.
- [Tooltip](templates/TooltipShowcase.md) (`TooltipShowcase`): 
- [Tooltip — Action Bar](templates/TooltipActionBarTooltips.md) (`TooltipActionBarTooltips`): Tooltips on an action button bar with contextual descriptions.
- [Tooltip — Hook Usage](templates/TooltipHookUsage.md) (`TooltipHookUsage`): Tooltip using the useTooltip hook for programmatic control.
- [Tooltip — Inline Text](templates/TooltipInlineTextTooltips.md) (`TooltipInlineTextTooltips`): Tooltips on inline text terms for definitions.
- [Top Nav](templates/shell-top-nav.md) (`shell-top-nav`): Application frame with horizontal navigation only: a centered bar whose items open full-width mega-menu panels, over placeholder content that keeps the entire width.
- [TopNav](templates/TopNavShowcase.md) (`TopNavShowcase`): 
- [TopNav — Centered Navigation](templates/TopNavCenteredNavigation.md) (`TopNavCenteredNavigation`): Navigation layout with center-aligned nav items flanked by a logo heading and end actions.
- [TopNav — Enterprise Dashboard](templates/TopNavEnterpriseDashboard.md) (`TopNavEnterpriseDashboard`): Full-featured navigation bar with icon-labeled nav items, search, notifications, and a primary CTA.
- [TopNav — Hover Menu](templates/TopNavHoverMenu.md) (`TopNavHoverMenu`): Navigation bar with a hover-triggered dropdown menu showing product items with icons and descriptions.
- [TopNav — Mega Menu](templates/TopNavMegaMenu.md) (`TopNavMegaMenu`): Marketing-style navigation with a full-width mega menu featuring product items and a promotional featured card.
- [TopNav — Multiple Dropdowns](templates/TopNavMultipleDropdowns.md) (`TopNavMultipleDropdowns`): Navigation bar with multiple hover-triggered dropdown menus that auto-close when switching between them.
- [TopNav — With Logo](templates/TopNavWithLogo.md) (`TopNavWithLogo`): Navigation bar with a branded logo icon, heading link, nav items, and a profile action.
- [TopNavHeading](templates/TopNavHeadingShowcase.md) (`TopNavHeadingShowcase`): Demonstrates TopNavHeading with a logo and text, both as a plain display and as a clickable link.
- [TopNavHeading — Basic](templates/TopNavHeadingBasic.md) (`TopNavHeadingBasic`): A product heading with a logo inside a TopNav, linked to the home page. Use as the leading brand element of a top navigation bar.
- [TopNavItem](templates/TopNavItemShowcase.md) (`TopNavItemShowcase`): Demonstrates TopNavItem with selected, icon, disabled, and default states.
- [TopNavItem — Basic](templates/TopNavItemBasic.md) (`TopNavItemBasic`): Navigation links inside a TopNav with one item marked as selected. Use for top-level pages of an application.
- [TopNavMegaMenu](templates/TopNavMegaMenuShowcase.md) (`TopNavMegaMenuShowcase`): Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenu with items and a featured card in the mega menu panel.
- [TopNavMegaMenu — Basic](templates/TopNavMegaMenuBasic.md) (`TopNavMegaMenuBasic`): A mega menu trigger inside a TopNav that opens a panel of rich link items. Use when a navigation section has multiple destinations worth describing.
- [TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard](templates/TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCardShowcase.md) (`TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCardShowcase`): Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard with a title, description, and CTA link inside a mega menu.
- [TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard — Basic](templates/TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCardBasic.md) (`TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCardBasic`): A promotional card with a title, description, and call-to-action link. Pass it to the featured slot of a TopNavMegaMenu to highlight announcements.
- [TopNavMegaMenuItem](templates/TopNavMegaMenuItemShowcase.md) (`TopNavMegaMenuItemShowcase`): Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenuItem with icons, titles, and descriptions inside a mega menu.
- [TopNavMegaMenuItem — Basic](templates/TopNavMegaMenuItemBasic.md) (`TopNavMegaMenuItemBasic`): Rich link items with an icon, title, and description. Use inside the items slot of a TopNavMegaMenu to describe each destination.
- [TopNavMenu](templates/TopNavMenuShowcase.md) (`TopNavMenuShowcase`): Demonstrates TopNavMenu with a hover-triggered dropdown containing items with icons and descriptions.
- [TopNavMenu — Basic](templates/TopNavMenuBasic.md) (`TopNavMenuBasic`): A dropdown menu inside a TopNav built from an items array with icons and descriptions. Use to group related destinations under a single trigger.
- [Tree List — Variants](templates/TreeListVariants.md) (`TreeListVariants`): The `variant` prop controls whether hierarchy guide lines are shown: `lineGuides` (default) draws connector lines between parent and child rows, while `noGuides` relies on indentation alone. It is orthogonal to `density`, which controls spacing.
- [Tree Table](templates/table-tree.md) (`table-tree`): Hierarchical table where every parent row rolls up from its children — a code repository whose folders show the newest commit beneath them, beside a detail sidebar and a rendered README. Columns resize, siblings sort within their own level, arrow keys walk the rows, and search prunes the tree to matching branches.
- [TreeList](templates/TreeListShowcase.md) (`TreeListShowcase`): 
- [TreeList — File Tree With Icons](templates/TreeListFileTreeWithIcons.md) (`TreeListFileTreeWithIcons`): File browser tree with folder and document icons distinguishing directories from files.
- [TreeList — Interactive Settings](templates/TreeListInteractiveSettings.md) (`TreeListInteractiveSettings`): Settings tree with clickable items and a documentation link.
- [TreeList — Mailbox Tree](templates/TreeListMailboxTree.md) (`TreeListMailboxTree`): Email folder tree with unread badge counts.
- [TreeList — Navigation Tree](templates/TreeListNavigationTree.md) (`TreeListNavigationTree`): Navigation tree with a selected item for the current page.
- [Two-column Form](templates/form-two-column.md) (`form-two-column`): Form split into two columns beneath a hero header: inputs on one flank, a persistent context panel opposite that stays put while the fields scroll. Flat, single submit, no steps.
- [Typeahead](templates/TypeaheadShowcase.md) (`TypeaheadShowcase`): 
- [Typeahead — Limited Results](templates/TypeaheadLimitedResults.md) (`TypeaheadLimitedResults`): Typeahead with a capped dropdown showing at most three results.
- [Typeahead — Search Field](templates/TypeaheadSearchField.md) (`TypeaheadSearchField`): Search input with icon and suggestions on focus.
- [Typeahead — With Helper Text](templates/TypeaheadWithHelperText.md) (`TypeaheadWithHelperText`): Typeahead with a description below the label.
- [Typeahead — With Validation](templates/TypeaheadWithValidation.md) (`TypeaheadWithValidation`): Typeahead with an error validation message.
- [TypeaheadItem](templates/TypeaheadItemShowcase.md) (`TypeaheadItemShowcase`): Typeahead with custom item rendering using TypeaheadItem for avatars and descriptions.
- [TypeaheadItem — Basic](templates/TypeaheadItemBasic.md) (`TypeaheadItemBasic`): A typeahead whose results are rendered with TypeaheadItem, adding a secondary description below each label. Use inside renderItem to keep custom results visually consistent.
- [useAnimator — Playing cards](templates/AnimatorPlayingCards.md) (`AnimatorPlayingCards`): A playing card that follows a drag: a gentle release springs it back on its release velocity, and a quick flick throws it away with momentum before the next card is dealt. A Discard button moves it off from the keyboard, fading it in place under Reduce Motion, and the discard is announced. Built only on the public useAnimator hook.
- [useAnnounce — Filter Result Count](templates/useAnnounceHookUsage.md) (`useAnnounceHookUsage`): A product filter that announces its result count with useAnnounce: once typing pauses for 500 ms, a screen reader hears "3 results" or "No results". The count has its own hasReplace instance, as the hook's docs advise for a changing value.
- [useAppShellMobile — Custom Mobile Trigger](templates/AppShellMobileHookUsage.md) (`AppShellMobileHookUsage`): Custom mobile navigation trigger built with useAppShellMobile. The trigger consumes the surrounding AppShell context instead of rendering its own shell.
- [useCalendarConstraints — Hotel Booking Range](templates/useCalendarConstraintsHookUsage.md) (`useCalendarConstraintsHookUsage`): A hotel booking range picker enforcing season min/max dates, a 7-night maximum stay once check-in is picked, and a custom rule disabling closed Mondays.
- [useCalendarDays — Month Grid](templates/useCalendarDaysHookUsage.md) (`useCalendarDaysHookUsage`): A compact custom month view: a seven-column table built from the weeks and dayNames that useCalendarDays returns, with only as many rows as the month needs. Days from the previous and next months are dimmed, and a Week starts on control (Sunday or Monday) reorders both the header and the grid.
- [useCalendarNavigation — Month Pager](templates/useCalendarNavigationHookUsage.md) (`useCalendarNavigationHookUsage`): A calendar month pager with previous/next navigation buttons, localized month-year label, and cross-month arrow key navigation using pendingFocus.
- [useClickableContainer — Clickable Project Card](templates/useClickableContainerHookUsage.md) (`useClickableContainerHookUsage`): A project card that useClickableContainer makes clickable anywhere: a click on the card follows its title link, while the Star button, the owner link and a text selection keep their own behavior, and Ctrl/Cmd+click or middle-click opens the project in a new tab.
- [useClipboard — Share Link](templates/useClipboardHookUsage.md) (`useClipboardHookUsage`): A share card that copies its invite link with useClipboard: the Copy button reads "Copied" while isCopied is true, a screen reader hears "Link copied", and a second press restarts the reset timer.
- [useCollapsible — Custom Disclosure](templates/CollapsibleHookUsage.md) (`CollapsibleHookUsage`): Custom disclosure UI built directly with useCollapsible for headless open/close state.
- [useCollator — Locale-aware Name Sort](templates/useCollatorHookUsage.md) (`useCollatorHookUsage`): A list of names sorted with the compare function from useCollator: accented and lowercase names land where a reader expects, and switching the provider locale to Swedish moves Å and Ö after Z.
- [useCombobox — Assign To Field](templates/useComboboxHookUsage.md) (`useComboboxHookUsage`): An "Assign to" TextInput and a list of Item rows, with the field, listbox and option props from useCombobox spread onto them: typing filters a list of teammates, ArrowUp and ArrowDown move the active option while focus stays in the input, Enter picks it and Escape closes the list.
- [useContainerReveal — Reveal-on-hover Row Actions](templates/useContainerRevealHookUsage.md) (`useContainerRevealHookUsage`): File rows keep their edit/delete actions hidden at rest and reveal them on hover or keyboard focus via useContainerReveal; the actions stay mounted and in the tab order.
- [useDragToSnapPoints — Playing card on three places](templates/DragToSnapPointsCard.md) (`DragToSnapPointsCard`): A playing card that a sideways drag moves between three places: a slow release settles on the nearest, a quick flick carries to the next, and a release moving back returns where it started. Buttons settle it from the keyboard, and the new place is announced. Built only on the public useDragToSnapPoints hook.
- [useFocusTrap — Quick Edit Panel](templates/useFocusTrapHookUsage.md) (`useFocusTrapHookUsage`): A custom quick-edit panel, not built on Dialog, that traps focus with useFocusTrap: focusFirst moves focus to its field on open, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it, Escape closes it through onEscape, and closing returns focus to the Quick edit button.
- [useGridFocus — Color Swatch Grid](templates/useGridFocusHookUsage.md) (`useGridFocusHookUsage`): A color swatch picker in rows of eight with one Tab stop. useGridFocus moves focus with the arrow keys, Home and End, and Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End. Each swatch is a button, so Enter or a click picks it.
- [useHotkeys — Search and Help Shortcuts](templates/useHotkeysHookUsage.md) (`useHotkeysHookUsage`): Page shortcuts registered with useHotkeys: "/" focuses the search field and "?" opens the shortcut help, while typing either character in the field just types it. A switch turns the single-key shortcuts off through isDisabled.
- [useHoverCard — Profile Preview](templates/HoverCardHookUsage.md) (`HoverCardHookUsage`): Custom profile preview using useHoverCard with direct trigger and render control.
- [useIcon — Status Row](templates/useIconHookUsage.md) (`useIconHookUsage`): A custom status row that draws the semantic success, warning and error icons with useIcon. The same row renders under the current theme and under a Theme whose icons override those three, and its icons change with no change to the component.
- [useImageMode — Photo Caption](templates/useImageModeHookUsage.md) (`useImageModeHookUsage`): A photo banner with a caption over the sky. useImageMode samples only the strip under the caption and MediaTheme switches the caption between light and dark text from the result. A Beach photo switch swaps a night photo for a bright beach photo, and while the new photo loads the caption keeps the dark fallback.
- [useInputContainer — Search Field Wrapper](templates/useInputContainerHookUsage.md) (`useInputContainerHookUsage`): A custom search field wrapper with a leading search icon, padding and a trailing Clear button. useInputContainer puts focus in the input when the icon or the padding is clicked, while a click on Clear empties the field without the wrapper taking it over.
- [useInputStatusIcon — Coupon Code Status](templates/useInputStatusIconHookUsage.md) (`useInputStatusIconHookUsage`): A custom bordered coupon-code input whose status affordance comes from useInputStatusIcon. A wrong code shows the error status and SAVE20 shows success. Switching the variant moves between a plain glyph with a message below (attached), no icon on the field (detached), and a focusable button whose tooltip keyboard and screen-reader users can reach, with its aria-describedby id returned by the hook (tooltip).
- [useInteractiveRole — One Tile, Four Roles](templates/useInteractiveRoleHookUsage.md) (`useInteractiveRoleHookUsage`): A polymorphic Tile used four ways: with an href it renders as a link, with an onClick as a button, with neither as plain content, and placed as a Popover trigger it becomes the trigger button through context — the resolution order in one place.
- [useKeyboardHint — Arrow-key Hint](templates/useKeyboardHintHookUsage.md) (`useKeyboardHintHookUsage`): A custom five-star rating with one Tab stop calls useKeyboardHint directly: tabbing into it shows a "← → to navigate" hint, the first arrow press dismisses it, and tabbing back in does not show it again.
- [useLayer — Anchored Layer](templates/LayerHookUsage.md) (`LayerHookUsage`): Low-level anchored overlay rendered with useLayer and a custom surface.
- [useLightbox — Gallery Grid](templates/LightboxHookUsage.md) (`LightboxHookUsage`): Photo gallery thumbnail grid using useLightbox for trigger props, keyboard navigation, and open state.
- [useLinkComponent — Article Cards](templates/useLinkComponentHookUsage.md) (`useLinkComponentHookUsage`): A custom Article card renders its title link with the component useLinkComponent resolves: the as prop first, then the nearest LinkProvider, then a native anchor. Inside a LinkProvider wired to a client-side router, the title navigates without a page load and updates the router location. With as="a" the title is a native anchor even inside the provider, and outside the provider it falls back to the next provider up or a native anchor.
- [useLinkify — Links in a Comment Thread](templates/useLinkifyHookUsage.md) (`useLinkifyHookUsage`): Plain-text comments where useLinkify turns the URL and the email address into Links, and a custom pattern turns issue references like #123 into tracker links — the patterns option in action. The comment without matches stays plain text.
- [useListFocus — Recent Files](templates/useListFocusHookUsage.md) (`useListFocusHookUsage`): A "Recent files" list of buttons with keyboard navigation from useListFocus: ArrowUp and ArrowDown move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last row, focus wraps at the ends, and only one row is in the tab order.
- [useLocale — Invoice Summary](templates/useLocaleHookUsage.md) (`useLocaleHookUsage`): An invoice summary that formats its date and amount with Intl using the locale from useLocale, so switching the provider from English to German changes "Nov 2, 2026" and "$1,234.50" to "2. Nov. 2026" and "1.234,50 $" with no second locale source.
- [useMergedRefs — AutoGrowTextArea](templates/useMergedRefsHookUsage.md) (`useMergedRefsHookUsage`): An AutoGrowTextArea that forwards the caller's ref and also keeps its own ref to measure scrollHeight. The merged ref attaches both to the same textarea: it resizes itself while a parent button focuses it through the forwarded ref.
- [useMultiCombobox — Issue Labels](templates/useMultiComboboxHookUsage.md) (`useMultiComboboxHookUsage`): A Labels field built on useMultiCombobox: typing filters the labels, the arrow keys move the active option while focus stays in the field, Enter or a click toggles a label and the list stays open, and selected labels show as removable tokens above the field.
- [useOutlineFromMarkdown — Docs Article](templates/useOutlineFromMarkdownHookUsage.md) (`useOutlineFromMarkdownHookUsage`): A docs-style article with an Outline next to it, built from the same Markdown string through useOutlineFromMarkdown. "Add section" appends a heading to the string, and a new entry that links to it appears in the outline.
- [useOverflow — Editor Toolbar](templates/useOverflowHookUsage.md) (`useOverflowHookUsage`): Resize the card: useOverflow moves the toolbar actions that do not fit into a More menu, and shows them again when the card gets wider.
- [useOverlay — Product Quick View](templates/useOverlayHookUsage.md) (`useOverlayHookUsage`): A product card that is its own overlay container: useOverlay returns the ref and props to spread on the Card and a bottom strip to render once over the image. Hovering the card, or moving keyboard focus into it, slides in a Quick view button along the bottom of the image, and leaving hides it again. The image is a link that the strip leaves clickable above it, and Tab lands on it first so the next Tab reaches Quick view.
- [usePanGesture — A draggable box](templates/PanDraggableBox.md) (`PanDraggableBox`): The smallest pan example, in two forms side by side: the usePanGesture hook and the createPanGesture factory. The factory takes any element, React or not. Each card names its API, follows a drag from a finger, a mouse or a pen, and springs back, with the same StyleX styles. A starting point for a draggable tile, a swipe or any drag-and-release gesture.
- [usePanGesture — A playing card (advanced)](templates/PanPlayingCard.md) (`PanPlayingCard`): An advanced usePanGesture example: a playing card follows a drag, settles back on a gentle release and flies off on a quick flick, while a Discard button deals the next card from the keyboard and announces it. Drag, settle and throw are StyleX styles driven by React state. A pattern for swipe-to-dismiss, card decks and flick gestures.
- [usePopover — Quick Actions](templates/PopoverHookUsage.md) (`PopoverHookUsage`): Custom quick-actions popover using usePopover for trigger refs, ARIA attributes, and focus trapping.
- [usePowerSearchConfig — Filtered Directory Table](templates/usePowerSearchConfigHookUsage.md) (`usePowerSearchConfigHookUsage`): A people directory with a PowerSearch bar over a Table: typed field definitions feed usePowerSearchConfig, returning the search config and an applyFilters helper that updates Table rows.
- [usePressFeedback — Pressable Card](templates/usePressFeedbackHookUsage.md) (`usePressFeedbackHookUsage`): A Card made pressable with usePressFeedback: its marker and the interactionOverlayStyles backgroundImage overlay go straight on the Card, so a press darkens the card the way every Astryx pressable does; focusOutlineStyles.focusVisible gives it the shared Astryx focus ring for keyboard focus; and a click, Enter or Space flips it.
- [useScrollableArea — Activity Log Panel](templates/useScrollableAreaHookUsage.md) (`useScrollableAreaHookUsage`): A fixed-height Activity log panel whose entries scroll up and down. useScrollableArea makes the panel a keyboard tab stop only when its entries overflow, reports which edges have more entries so a top or bottom shadow shows only there, and keeps a scroll that reaches the end from scrolling the page. Add entry flips the panel from not scrollable to scrollable.
- [useScrollLock — Full-screen Mobile Menu](templates/useScrollLockHookUsage.md) (`useScrollLockHookUsage`): A custom full-screen menu opened from a Menu button. useScrollLock pins the page behind it while it is open, so the page does not scroll or shift sideways, and closing the menu returns the reader to the same scroll position.
- [useScrollOverflow — Filter Strip Edge Fades](templates/useScrollOverflowHookUsage.md) (`useScrollOverflowHookUsage`): A row of active filters that scrolls sideways. useScrollOverflow reports which edge has hidden filters, and the strip fades only that edge: none while every filter fits, the end at the start, both mid-scroll and the start at the end. Adding or removing a filter updates the fades, and in a right-to-left layout the start edge is on the right.
- [useSnapPaging — Onboarding Pages](templates/CarouselSnapPaging.md) (`CarouselSnapPaging`): Onboarding cards in a Carousel with hasSnap={useSnapPaging()}: under a finger or a trackpad swipe, each flick moves one view and rests on a card's start edge. A switch picks one view or one card per flick through the hook's pages option.
- [useStreamingText — Streaming Response](templates/useStreamingTextHookUsage.md) (`useStreamingTextHookUsage`): A chat-style reply card: while the response streams in bursts, useStreamingText reveals it steadily character by character; when streaming ends the full text snaps into place. Regenerate replays the stream.
- [useTableColumnResize — Draggable Columns](templates/ColumnResizeHookUsage.md) (`ColumnResizeHookUsage`): A Table using useTableColumnResize. Drag the right edge of any column header to resize; widths are committed on release. The last proportional column flexes to fill remaining space.
- [useTableColumnSettingsState — Column Visibility Picker](templates/useTableColumnSettingsStateHookUsage.md) (`useTableColumnSettingsStateHookUsage`): A Table toolbar with a Columns menu of checkboxes: toggling Email updates active columns, Reset restores defaults, and the config is passed directly to useTableColumnSettings.
- [useTableGroupedRows — Collapsible Groups](templates/TableGroupedRowsTable.md) (`TableGroupedRowsTable`): A table grouped into collapsible sections with useTableGroupedRows. Each group gets a full-width header with a chevron, label, and member count; click to collapse/expand.
- [useTableRowExpansion — Tree Table](templates/TableRowExpansionTable.md) (`TableRowExpansionTable`): A tree table using useTableRowExpansion with inherited columns. Child rows use the same columns as parents, indented by depth. Click the chevron or right-click to expand/collapse.
- [useTableRowIndex — Numbered Rows](templates/TableRowIndexTable.md) (`TableRowIndexTable`): A table with a prepended row-number column via useTableRowIndex. Numbering is monospaced, right-aligned, and follows the rows the table renders.
- [useTableRowStatus - Semantic and Custom Markers](templates/TableRowStatusTable.md) (`TableRowStatusTable`): A job table using both row-status paths: status resolves themed semantic glyphs and tones, while color stays a custom paint choice with an optional caller-selected icon or the stable dot.
- [useTableRowsVirtualization - Fixed Height Rows](templates/RowsVirtualizationHookUsage.md) (`RowsVirtualizationHookUsage`): A Table with 1,000 product rows inside a 320px-tall parent, which bounds its scroll area. Give the Table's parent a height, fixed or relative, or a flex child, so windowing can bound the rows; with no height every row renders. Scroll vertically to mount the visible rows. The caller keeps all data and columns; this hook does not virtualize columns.
- [useTableSortableState — Multi-Sort Orders](templates/useTableSortableStateHookUsage.md) (`useTableSortableStateHookUsage`): Orders with no sort code of their own: useTableSortableState owns the sort state, returns the sorted orders, and hands useTableSortable a ready config. Click Customer, then Shift-click Total, to sort by customer and then by total within each customer. A line above the orders reads the current sort state from the hook.
- [useTableStickyColumns — Pinned Columns](templates/StickyColumnsHookUsage.md) (`StickyColumnsHookUsage`): A Table using useTableStickyColumns to pin the Name column to the start edge and Status to the end edge. Scroll horizontally; pinned columns stay in view with a soft shadow over the scrolling content.
- [useTableTreeData: Tree Table](templates/TableTreeTable.md) (`TableTreeTable`): A file-tree table built from nested data. useTableTreeState flattens the tree into the visible rows and owns the expanded set; useTableTreeData draws the per-level indent and the expand/collapse chevron in the tree column. The two hooks are designed to work together, so this one example covers both. hasExpandAllControl adds the expand-all/collapse-all toggle to the tree column header. Collapsed branches are unmounted, not hidden.
- [useTheme — Token Values](templates/useThemeHookUsage.md) (`useThemeHookUsage`): Read resolved theme token values with useTheme for non-CSS consumers like SVG charts.
- [useToast — Settings Saved](templates/useToastHookUsage.md) (`useToastHookUsage`): Shows a toast from the function useToast returns: a "Settings saved" confirmation with an Undo action, a uniqueID so pressing the button again replaces the toast instead of stacking another, and an error toast when the request fails.
- [useTranslator — Load More Footer](templates/useTranslatorHookUsage.md) (`useTranslatorHookUsage`): A "Load more" footer under a list that gets its button label and its "Showing 3 of 9" count from the function useTranslator returns, with app message keys supplied per locale through InternationalizationProvider, so switching the provider to French changes both strings.
- [useTreeFocus — Keyboard File Tree](templates/useTreeFocusHookUsage.md) (`useTreeFocusHookUsage`): A custom file tree built from plain rows with tree roles. useTreeFocus gives it the WAI-ARIA tree keyboard model: ArrowUp and ArrowDown move over the visible rows, ArrowRight opens a folder or moves into it, ArrowLeft closes it or moves to its parent, Home and End jump to the ends, a typed letter jumps to a matching name, Enter opens a file, and only one row is in the tab order.
- [useTypeahead — Type to Focus a Country](templates/useTypeaheadHookUsage.md) (`useTypeaheadHookUsage`): A country list of buttons with useListFocus arrow keys and useTypeahead type-to-focus. Typing "can" focuses Canada, pressing "b" again and again cycles through Belgium, Brazil and Bulgaria, and "e" finds Éire with the accent ignored. The hook only reports the match through onMatch, and useListFocus moves focus.
- [Vertical Wizard](templates/form-wizard-vertical.md) (`form-wizard-vertical`): Multi-step wizard with the steps in a fixed left rail that stays visible while the form scrolls, plus a side panel whose guidance follows the focused field. Suits long or unequal steps carrying uploads, previews, and dense review metadata. As width tightens the guidance drops first, then the rail rotates into a horizontal stepper above the form.
- [VisuallyHidden](templates/VisuallyHiddenShowcase.md) (`VisuallyHiddenShowcase`): 
- [VisuallyHidden — Live Region](templates/VisuallyHiddenLiveRegion.md) (`VisuallyHiddenLiveRegion`): A polite aria-live region announces visual-only state changes to assistive technology.
- [VisuallyHidden — Structural Heading](templates/VisuallyHiddenStructuralHeading.md) (`VisuallyHiddenStructuralHeading`): Give a visually implicit section an accessible name so screen-reader users can navigate to it.
- [VisuallyHidden — Supplementary Context](templates/VisuallyHiddenSupplementaryContext.md) (`VisuallyHiddenSupplementaryContext`): Stat cards whose trend arrows get screen-reader-only text, so a change like +12% is read as an increase from last month. Use to make terse visual data accessible.
- [VStack](templates/VStackShowcase.md) (`VStackShowcase`): Demonstrates VStack arranging items vertically with different gaps.
- [VStack — Basic](templates/VStackBasic.md) (`VStackBasic`): A heading and paragraphs stacked vertically with a consistent gap. Use VStack whenever siblings should flow top to bottom with even spacing.
- [Width budget: pixels or any CSS length](templates/DrawerWidths.md) (`DrawerWidths`): Compare a numeric pixel width with rem and percentage lengths. The width budget also caps the drawer on mobile.
- [With close button](templates/DrawerHeaderWithCloseButton.md) (`DrawerHeaderWithCloseButton`): Pass onOpenChange to render a close button that calls it with false. Drawer renders no close button of its own, so this is the usual visible way to close.
- [With subtitle and end content](templates/DrawerHeaderSubtitleEndContent.md) (`DrawerHeaderSubtitleEndContent`): Add a subtitle under the title and put a status, such as a Badge, in endContent. The close button stays at the end of the row.
- [Work Item Detail](templates/work-item-detail.md) (`work-item-detail`): Single work-item detail in two columns: a title with a status selector, a description, a subtask checklist with progress, an attachments block, and a comment and activity feed in the main column, plus a property rail with assignee, dates, labels, and linked items. The shape for any tracked item with children, properties, and a comment history — a task, ticket, issue, story, bug, card, request, or work item.

## Docs topics

- [author-a-theme](topics/author-a-theme.md): Create, customize, and build a theme: defineTheme, palette generation, token overrides, component style overrides, custom variants, responsive adaptations, and production builds.
- [browser-support](topics/browser-support.md): What browsers Astryx targets, which modern platform features it depends on, and how to support older browsers for your own audience.
- [color](topics/color.md): Semantic color tokens for surfaces, text, icons, borders, and status indicators.
- [elevation](topics/elevation.md): Shadow tokens for visual elevation and inset state rings.
- [getting-started](topics/getting-started.md): Add the design system to your project and start building.
- [icons](topics/icons.md): Semantic icon names available in the design system. These adapt to the active theme's icon registry.
- [illustrations](topics/illustrations.md): Illustration guidelines for empty states, onboarding flows, and feature highlights.
- [is-my-code-good](topics/is-my-code-good.md): Check whether a product surface fits its app and uses Astryx well, require evidence for every claim, and improve it with a repeatable agent review.
- [motion](topics/motion.md): Duration and easing tokens for animations and transitions.
- [principles](topics/principles.md): Core design principles and rules for building with the design system.
- [shape](topics/shape.md): Border radius tokens for consistent component rounding, from sharp corners to full pills.
- [spacing](topics/spacing.md): Spacing scale tokens for padding, gap, and margin: the rhythmic foundation of design system layouts.
- [styling-overview](topics/styling-overview.md): How to set up CSS — exact imports for three paths: plain, Tailwind, and StyleX for your own code — plus the stylesheet each Astryx package ships.
- [theme](topics/theme.md): How to use and create themes: see Use a theme for applying themes, and Author a theme for creating and customizing them.
- [use-a-theme](topics/use-a-theme.md): Apply a theme to your app: install, import with the CLI, wire the generated module, switch dark mode, nest themes, and choose runtime or built for production.
- [use-integrations](topics/use-integrations.md): Install, discover, and use integration packages that add components, templates, themes, and docs to your app.
- [working-with-ai](topics/working-with-ai.md): How to set up AI coding tools to generate correct component code.
